with large amount of entities to process

before being processed, potentially causing memory issues if the list is
too large, while asyncio.queue doesn't require holding all items in
memory at once.

# Description

The genesis of this change is documented in this [slack
thread](https://port-community.slack.com/archives/C06UR5F2WCX/p1717488013161949)

**What** 
- Users encounter a 400 error when attempting to create subscriptions
(webhooks) due to insufficient permissions to edit the subscription.
- Modify the webhook creation process to include the projectId in the
payload.

**Why** 
- The current setup assumes an organisation token when creating
webhooks. If a project-scoped token is supplied, the craetion fails


**How**
- When the user holds a project administrator role, and the PAT is
scoped only to that specific project, it is necessary to explicitly
define the projectId when creating a webhook.
```json
{
  "publisherId": "tfs",
  "eventType": "git.pullrequest.updated",
  "consumerId": "webHooks",
  "consumerActionId": "httpRequest",

  },
  "publisherInputs": {
    "projectId": "4901a905-d07b-4027-b7cc-577d2b6a0e31"

}
```

[Integration][AWS] throw error if no permissions on region (#889)

# Description

What - We have implemented blacklist error handling for AWS errors in
our system. This ensures that certain AWS error types are specifically
caught and handled differently from other errors.

Why - Each AWS resource handles "not found" errors differently, making
it challenging to distinguish between a resource not being found and an
actual error in the system. This inconsistency can lead to
misinterpretation of errors and inappropriate error handling. By adding
blacklist error handling, we can provide more accurate and consistent
error handling across different AWS resources.

How - We have introduced a blacklist mechanism that explicitly catches
specific AWS error codes related to "not found" scenarios. These error
codes are then handled separately from other types of errors, allowing
us to treat them as non-critical issues and proceed accordingly. This
ensures that our system can gracefully handle situations where AWS
resources are legitimately not found without mistaking them for system
errors. This approach improves our system's robustness and reliability
in interacting with AWS services.

message: [ADO] Add work items to get issues, tasks, and epics (#893) # Description This PR introduces the functionality to retrieve issues, tasks, and epics from Azure DevOps (ADO) projects within the organization. The implementation involves a two-step process to efficiently fetch the required data: **Fetch Work Item IDs using WIQL:** A WIQL (Work Item Query Language) query is executed to retrieve the IDs of the work items (issues, tasks, and epics) that match the specified criteria. This step helps optimize data retrieval by fetching only the necessary IDs, avoiding unnecessary data transfer. **Fetch Detailed Work Item Data:** Using the obtained work item IDs, the API is called to fetch the complete details of each work item. Batch processing is employed to handle potential API limitations on the number of IDs that can be fetched in a single request. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## Screenshots Include screenshots from your environment showing how the resources of the integration will look. ## API Documentation Provide links to the API documentation used for this integration.

message:
[Integration][GCP] Added an alternative for retrieving quota project id (#997) # Description **What** This PR fixes a bug related to fetching the GCP project ID from service account credentials. Previously, the function would fail to retrieve the correct project ID when the `quota_project_id` key was missing from the credentials file. **Why** GCP configuration differs based on how the credentials are generated. When using `gcloud auth application-default login`, the project ID is stored under the `quota_project_id` key. However, when a service account key is generated from the console, the project ID is stored under the `project_id` key. This discrepancy caused the integration to fail in identifying the project ID when the credentials were generated from the console, impacting quota computation operations. This bug affected users by causing failures in environments where `quota_project_id` was not available. message: [Integration][AWS] | Improved Concurrency Control and Eliminated Likelihood of Thundering Herd (#1063) # Description **What:** - Refactored semaphore implementation to effectively limit concurrency across tasks. - Added a util `semaphore_async_iterator` to enable seamless control over concurrent executions per kind (can be re-used in other integrations). - Removed iterative calls to the cache for tracking token expiry, reducing the likelihood of a thundering herd problem. **Why:** - The previous implementation limited concurrency within tasks (accounts), ideally, this use case requires concurrent limits is to be global, thus across accounts. - Iterative cache calls could potentially cause a thundering herd problem when cache expires and token needed to be refreshed. **How:** - Applied the semaphore correctly by wrapping task creation with the semaphore, ensuring proper concurrency control. - Implemented unit tests using `pytest` to verify semaphore functionality and concurrency limits. - subject: [Integration][Snyk] - Validation to Prevent Fetching Non Existent Users (#1098)
message:
[Integration][Snyk] - Validation to Prevent Fetching Non Existent Users (#1098) # Description What - Customers had the impression that the integration was bringing data from other organizations that were not specified during the installation process. The particular cause of concern was the Snyk API that enriches the project data with the importer and owner details. It is possible that an importer or the owner of the Snyk project have left the organization. In this instance, when we query the API, we will get 404, which is expected. But the fact that the customer sees an API call to the owners new organization makes it appear that the integration is pulling data from other org. Why - How - Added validation to prevent the integration from making attempts to fetch users from other organisation instead of the ones provided to the integration ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Gitlab] Made event processing sequential to temporarily resolve race condition issues (#1217)
message:
[Integration][Gitlab] Made event processing sequential to temporarily resolve race condition issues (#1217) # Description **What** - Updated the event handling logic in both `EventHandler` and `SystemEventHandler` to ensure sequential processing of observers and hook handlers. - Removed concurrent execution (`asyncio.gather` and `asyncio.create_task`) and replaced it with sequential execution. **Why** - The previous implementation processed events concurrently across multiple observers and hook handlers, which led to race conditions when shared entities were updated. - This caused data inconsistency, as concurrent updates overwrote each other's changes. - Sequential processing ensures that each observer and handler processes the event one at a time, maintaining data integrity. **How** 1. `EventHandler` Changes: - Replaced `asyncio.create_task` for observer notifications with a direct `await` call. - Ensured observers for a specific event are processed in a sequential manner. 2. `SystemEventHandler` Changes: - Removed `asyncio.gather` for hook handlers and replaced it with nested `for` loops. - Handlers are now invoked sequentially for each client, ensuring predictable and ordered execution. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Core] JQ Mapping log enrichment - empty values support (#1285)
message:
[Core] JQ Mapping log enrichment - empty values support (#1285)

# Description

What -
added test and support for use-case of empty string of
identifier/blueprint values,
added debug log to validate the identifier and blueprint values
Why -
I've identified that there are 2 main use-cases for us to log the
details about, for null, missing and / or mis configured values
AND for empty strings. 
the empty string is not a "wrong / misconfigured" value for JQ, but it
is a non valid identifier.
current logs were missing this details and were not clear enough
also added example on how to assert on logs
How -

message:
[Core] add the abstract class and context function (#1337) # Description # Standardized Webhook Processing Implementation ## Description This PR introduces a standardized webhook processing system that provides a robust, consistent way to handle webhook events across the application. The implementation includes retry logic, queue management, and graceful shutdown capabilities. ## Key Components ### 1. Abstract Webhook Handler - Base class `AbstractWebhookHandler` that defines the contract for webhook processing - Built-in retry mechanism with exponential backoff - Customizable hooks for initialization, teardown, and error handling - Support for authentication and payload validation ### 2. Webhook Handler Manager - Centralized management of webhook routes and handlers - Asynchronous queue-based processing - Support for multiple handlers per path with filtering capabilities - Graceful shutdown with configurable timeouts ### 3. Queue System - Abstract queue interface for flexibility in implementation - Default `LocalQueue` implementation using `asyncio.Queue` - Support for tracking and managing webhook processing state ## Features - **Retry Logic**: Configurable retry attempts with exponential backoff - **Filtering**: Support for handler-specific event filtering - **Queue Management**: Ordered processing of webhook events - **Graceful Shutdown**: Proper cleanup of resources and in-flight requests - **Extensibility**: Easy to add new webhook handlers and customize behavior - **Monitoring**: Built-in logging and timing metrics ## Example Usage ```python class CustomWebhookHandler(AbstractWebhookHandler): async def authenticate(self, payload: EventPayload, headers: Dict[str, str]) -> bool: # Custom authentication logic return True async def validate_payload(self, payload: EventPayload) -> bool: # Custom validation logic return True async def handle_event(self, payload: EventPayload) -> None: # Custom event handling logic pass ``` ## Register handler with optional filter ```python ocean.add_handler("/webhook/path", CustomWebhookHandler, filter_function) ``` ## Configuration Options - `max_retries`: Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 3) - `initial_retry_delay_seconds`: Initial delay between retries (default: 1.0) - `max_retry_delay_seconds`: Maximum delay between retries (default: 30.0) - `exponential_base_seconds`: Base for exponential backoff (default: 2.0) ## Impact - Standardizes webhook handling across the application - Improves reliability through retry mechanisms - Provides better control over webhook processing - Enables monitoring and debugging through consistent logging ### Request process 1. Initial Request Reception - FastAPI route receives the HTTP POST request - Request is converted to a WebhookEvent object - Event is timestamped and added to the path-specific queue - Returns immediate response to caller (async processing) 2. Queue Processing - Dedicated queue processor continuously monitors the queue - When an event arrives, it's retrieved from the queue - Processing context is established with logging 3. Handler Selection & Execution - Finds handlers registered for the path that match the event filter - Creates instance of the matching handler 4. Event Processing - Validates webhook setup - Authenticates the request - Validates the payload - Attempts to handle the event with retry logic: - If error occurs and is retryable, waits and retries - If max retries exceeded or non-retryable error, fails 5. Completion - Sets final timestamp based on success/failure - Marks item as processed in queue - Logs processing completion with timing information ``` Request → Queue (immediate response) → Queue Processor picks up event → Handler Selection → Setup Validation → Authentication → Payload Validation → Event Processing (with potential retries) → Success/Failure Logging → Cleanup ``` This architecture ensures: - Non-blocking request handling - Ordered processing per path - Reliable retry mechanism - Proper resource cleanup - Comprehensive logging - Graceful error handling ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][AWS] | Fix InvalidToken Exceptions Due to Improper Token Refresh Calls (#1190)
message:
[Integration][AWS] | Fix InvalidToken Exceptions Due to Improper Token Refresh Calls (#1190) # Description **What:** We've encountered timeouts and InvalidToken exceptions despite implementing a time-based token refresh strategy designed to refresh the token when it's 80% close to expiry, this occurs arbitrarily. **Why:** The token refresh may not be occurring at the appropriate points in the application. It appears that the refresh is triggered while an active session is still utilizing the old token. When the token is replaced during an ongoing session, the active session becomes obsolete, leading to InvalidToken exceptions. The session refresh call is placed incorrectly within the application flow. Active sessions are not updated with the new token after a refresh, causing them to fail when attempting to access AWS resources. **How (Proposed Solution):** Review and adjust the placement of the token refresh logic to ensure it does not interfere with active sessions. Implement a check to verify if a session's token is valid or has a significant amount of time remaining before each resource (kind) retrieval operation. Ensure that new tokens are only used for new sessions, or gracefully handle the transition for active sessions. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Azure Devops] Fixed Incorrect Pagination In Work-Items Resource Retrieval (#1383)
message:
[Integration][Azure Devops] Fixed Incorrect Pagination In Work-Items Resource Retrieval (#1383) # Description **What** Implemented pagination for fetching work items in the Azure DevOps integration. Instead of retrieving all work items (up to 19,999) in a single request, the change splits the work item IDs into smaller, manageable batches using an asynchronous generator. Each batch is then processed individually, and project details are appended to each work item. **Why** Previously, the integration fetched all work items in one go, leading to performance issues and delayed live data updates during the resync process. This change improves the overall performance by reducing the amount of data processed per API call, thus ensuring smoother resync operations and faster live updates. **How** - Refactored the `generate_work_items` method to iterate over work item IDs in paginated batches. - Refactored the `_fetch_work_items_in_batches` method to an async generator which retrieves work items in batches defined by `page_size` (defaulting to the API maximum of 200). - Ensured that each batch of work items is enriched with project details before being yielded. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Gitlab] Fix Memory Leak Identified In Live Events Sync (#1371)
message:
[Integration][Gitlab] Fix Memory Leak Identified In Live Events Sync (#1371) ##Description What Currently, when a live event is received, we pass a deep copy of the event object to each observer. This was originally implemented to ensure that every observer received its own, uniquely referenced copy of the event. However, in our current workflow, observers do not modify the event data—they only use it to fetch resources from GitLab. Why - Since the observers only perform read operations (i.e., fetching data) and do not modify the event object, creating deep copies is redundant. - It has been observed that the deep‑copied objects are not being garbage collected after use, which results in increased memory usage and could eventually lead to memory exhaustion. - The deep copy operation introduces additional processing time and memory overhead that is not needed given the current use case. How - Modify the event handling logic to pass the original event object (or a shallow copy if absolutely necessary for safety) to observers instead of performing a deep copy. - Since observers only read from the event data, they can safely operate on the same shared object without risking race conditions or data corruption. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Gitlab] Fix File Search Logging to only log when no files found (#1456) # Description **What -** This PR updates the asynchronous file search logic by introducing a flag (`files_found`) to track whether any matching files are yielded during iteration. If no files are found, it logs an appropriate message. **Why -** Previously, the `async for...else` construct always executed the `else` block, causing a log message to be printed even when files were successfully found. The new approach ensures that the log message is only triggered when no files match the search patterns. **How -** 1. A boolean flag `files_found` is initialized to `False` before starting the asynchronous iteration. 2. As files are yielded by the asynchronous generator, the flag is set to `True`. 3. After the iteration completes, the flag is checked. If no files were found (`files_found` is still `False`), a log message is issued indicating that no matching files were found. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][AWS] Resolve Cloud Control Pagination Issue (#1453)
message:
[Integration][AWS] Resolve Cloud Control Pagination Issue (#1453) # Description **What** - This PR fixes an issue in the AWS integration where the API returns only 1000 resources in a single batch for the SQS Kind, despite the MaxResults parameter being set, and no NextToken is provided to paginate through all available resources. - Some resources have uncontrollable numbers of resources retrieved per paginated request. **Why** The current behavior leads to incomplete ingestion (e.g., tests made it clear that, only 1000 out of 1500 SQS queues available are processed) since the MaxResults parameter is ignored and subsequent pages cannot be retrieved. This bug, observed on the AWS SQS kind and potentially affecting other resources using the cloudcontrol API, needs to be resolved to ensure that all resources are ingested as expected. **How** - Introduced a custom pagination utility `AsyncPaginator` to better manage paginated API requests. - Modified the integration to detach SQS from the cloudcontrol API, addressing the missing `NextToken` issue that previously prevented further pagination. - The new utility ensures that regardless of the response from the API, the given Batch Size is respected during pagination. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][Gitlab] Improve Memory Usage For Members Kind (#1502)
message:
[Integration][Gitlab] Improve Memory Usage For Members Kind (#1502) # Description **What** This PR optimizes our group member synchronization by ensuring that only unique group members are stored and processed. In addition, caching for groups has been removed to reduce memory overhead. **Why** The previous implementation accumulated all group members during pagination, which naturally led to higher memory usage for groups with many members (an O(n) space complexity). Although there was no memory leak, this design resulted in a peak usage during member syncing. With the optimization—deduplicating members in each batch—the peak memory usage was reduced from 105 MB to 84 MB when syncing 30 unique inherited members. **How** - **Batch Processing:** The member enrichment now processes members in batches, filtering out duplicates on the fly before adding them to the final list. - **Deduplication:** For each batch, the process checks member IDs and ensures only unique members are stored, reducing unnecessary memory consumption. - **Caching Removal:** The caching mechanism on the `get_all_groups` method has been removed, lowering the overall memory footprint. - **Logging Enhancements:** Improved logging provides better visibility into the number of processed members per group and overall progress during syncing. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Gitlab] - Initialise Gitlab v2 Integration (#1442) # Description # What This PR introduces the initial release (0.1.0-dev) of the GitLab v2 integration, enabling synchronization of GitLab data—Groups, Projects, Issues, Merge Requestsinto the Port catalog. This implementation includes: - **Authentication Setup**: Initializes token-based authentication for GitLab API access. - **Client Structure**: Establishes a `GitLabClient` that uses a `RestClient` for all API interactions. - **Data Synchronization**: Fetches Groups, Projects, Issues, and Merge Requests from GitLab using REST endpoints. - **Label Fetch and Mapping Option**: Fetches project labels and maps them to a `__labels` field only if the `include_labels` configuration is enabled, with a similar `include_languages` option for language data. # Why The purpose of this integration is to minimize technical debt by creating an efficient and maintainable solution for GitLab synchronization # How The implementation is structured as follows, with memory usage data highlighting its efficiency: - **Authentication Setup**: The `AuthClient` in `clients/auth_client.py` manages GitLab API tokens, generating Bearer headers for all requests. This ensures secure and consistent API access. - **Client Structure**: The `GitLabClient` in `clients/gitlab_client.py` handles API interactions, delegating all requests to `RestClient`. - **REST Queries**: The `RestClient` targets all GitLab endpoints (e.g., `projects`, `groups`, `issues`, `merge_requests`, `labels`) with a default batch size of 100,Projects are fetched with optional enrichment for languages and labels based on configuration flags. - **Label Fetch and Mapping**: Project labels are fetched via REST only if the `include_labels` flag in `integration.py` is enabled. When fetched, labels are mapped to a `__labels` field in the output. Similarly, languages are mapped to `__languages` when `include_languages` is enabled. - **Memory Usage Data**: The memory usage graph demonstrates that `gitlab-v2-dev` (yellow) operates with a low memory footprint, averaging approximately 100 GB during idle periods and peaking at around 150 GB during active synchronization (e.g., 01:41:00-01:44:00). In contrast, `gitlab-dev` (green) averages around 200 GB and peaks at 250 GB during the same period, while `jira-dev` (blue) remains below 100 GB, indicating that this integration uses fewer memory resources than its predecessor while maintaining effective synchronization. ![PerformanceOptGQL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3b6a15a-f600-40a3-9528-d06686987b8d) ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [x] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Integration][Gitlab-V2] Added Live Events Support (#1524) **Overview:** This pull request adds live events support to Gitlab V2 Integration. Currently, it supports configuring Group Webhooks for a variety of events and is designed to be extendable to Project and System Webhooks in the future through the `BaseWebhookFactory` class. **What Changed:** - **Live Events Integration:** - Implements GitLab Group Webhooks for key events: - Merge Requests - Issues - Releases - Subgroups - Push Events - Tag Pushes - **Webhook Factories & Processors:** - Added factories to create webhook configurations at the group level. - Introduced processors to handle GitLab events such as merge requests, issues, and pushes. - **Client Enhancements:** - Extended the GitLab client with additional API methods for projects, groups, issues, and merge requests. - Incorporated custom exceptions and utility enums for better error handling and configuration. **Why This Update?** The enhancement supports incoming webhook integrations for our ocean integrations, ensuring that the system can process live GitLab events efficiently. This real-time event handling improves the responsiveness and robustness of our integration framework. **How It Was Implemented:** - **Design:** - Follows GitLab’s Webhook architecture as outlined in their [documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/development/webhooks.html). - Focuses on Group Webhooks with the flexibility to extend to other webhook types (e.g [System Hook](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/system_hooks/), [Projects Hook](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/project_webhooks/)) via a common base class. - **Testing:** - Extensive test coverage has been added to validate: - Creation, updating, and deletion of entities. - Successful resync operations. - Handling of multiple integrations and event listener configurations (Kafka and Polling). - Both core and integration test checklists have been met, ensuring robust quality assurance. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Gitlab-v2] Added support for file kind (#1482) # Description ## What - Added support for syncing file data from GitLab to Port within the GitLab integration. - Introduced file content fetching and parsing (JSON/YAML) in the GitLab client. - Enabled file search across repositories and groups using GitLab’s advanced search syntax with `scope` and `query`. ## Why Enable users to sync and manage file-based data from GitLab in Port. ## How - **Client Updates (`gitlab_client.py`):** - Added `get_file_content` and `file_exists` for retrieving and checking file existence. - Introduced `search_files` to search for files using `scope` (e.g., `"blobs"`) and `query`, supporting GitLab’s advanced search syntax across repositories and groups. - **Parsing Logic (`utils.py`):** - Added `parse_file_content` to parse JSON and YAML file content into structured data. - **Entity Processing:** - Extended processing in `file_entity_processor.py` to handle `file://` references by fetching and parsing file content. ### Integration Updates: - **GitLabFileProcessor:** - Added to process `file://` references in entity mappings, fetching content - Added to process `search://` references in entity mappings, checking file existence. - **GitLabFilesResourceConfig (`integration.py`):** - Introduced `query` field to configure file searches using GitLab’s advanced search syntax. - **Integration and Main Updates (`main.py`):** - Added `on_resync_files` handler to sync files using `scope="blobs"` and user-defined queries. ### Utilities and Improvements: - **Utility Functions (`utils.py`):** - Included `parse_file_content` for JSON/YAML parsing. - Assumed `get_file_paths` in `gitops/utils.py` to extract file paths from entity mappings (if applicable). --- ### Notes for PR Reviewers - **Feature Focus**: This PR enables file syncing with query-based search (e.g., `"filename:config.yaml"`, `"test"`) instead of pattern matching. - **Scope**: Currently uses `scope="blobs"` for file searches; future enhancements could expand to other scopes. - **Config**: Users must update file kind configs to use `query` instead of glob patterns for file searches in gitlab-v2 ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

**Real-Time File Change Processing**: Introduced a GitLab file push webhook processor to handle file changes as they happen in GitLab repositories. ## Why - **Optimized Resource Usage**: Reduced the risk of API rate limit errors and improved the overall performance of GitLab resource fetching. - message:
[Integration][AWS] AWS Integration Performance, Log and Memory Optimization (#1549) # Description ## What This PR improves memory management and performance of the AWS integration by: - Implementing early detection for filtered regions to prevent unnecessary processing - Reducing the number of AWS clients created during resource fetching - Processing accounts synchronously to better manage memory usage ## Why The AWS integration has been experiencing two main issues: 1. **High memory consumption** during resync operations, which can lead to performance degradation 2. **Misleading logs** that show regions being processed even when they're filtered out by region policies, creating confusion ## How The changes address these issues through several key improvements: 1. **Early Region Filtering**: - Implemented early detection for filtered regions before attempting to process them - Only allowed regions now iterate over account resources, reducing unnecessary processing 2. **Optimized Client Creation**: - Reduced the number of AWS clients created in `resync_cloudcontrol` and other resource fetching utilities - This minimizes memory overhead from client connections 3. **Synchronous Account Processing**: - Modified the integration to process accounts synchronously rather than in parallel - This provides better control over memory usage and prevents resource exhaustion ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][AWS] Add AWS Resource Groups Member Resources Support (#1548)
message:
[Integration][AWS] Add AWS Resource Groups Member Resources Support (#1548) # Description ## What Added support for handling `AWS::ResourceGroups::Group` as a special kind, allowing optional resyncing of associated group resources. This improvement facilitates the relationship between individual resources and their respective resource groups. ## Why Resource groups in AWS are a powerful way to organize and manage related resources. Currently, the integration only syncs the resource groups themselves without their member resources, which limits the ability to establish relationships between resources and their groups. By adding support for syncing member resources, we can create a more comprehensive view of the AWS environment and enable better resource management through Port. ## How 1. Implemented a new `resync_resource_group` function that fetches resource groups and their member resources 2. Created helper functions `fetch_group_resources` and `enrich_group_with_resources` to handle the retrieval and enrichment of group resources 3. Added a configuration option `list_group_resources` to control whether member resources should be included 4. Updated the `resync_resource_groups` function in `main.py` to use the new implementation 5. Added comprehensive tests for all new functions 6. subject: [Integration][Wiz] Added retry mechanisim for transient error (#1605)
message:
[Integration][Wiz] Added retry mechanisim for transient error (#1605) # Description **What** This PR fixes a bug in the Wiz integration where connection errors, such as `ConnectError: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution`, were not retried during GraphQL queries. It adds a test to verify the retry behavior and updates the `make_graphql_query` method to include the `extensions={"retryable": True}` parameter. **Why** The `make_graphql_query` method in `WizClient` was not configured to retry transient connection errors, leading to failures when temporary network issues occurred (e.g., DNS resolution failures). The error traceback showed a `ConnectError` during an HTTP POST request to the Wiz API, which disrupted the application's functionality. Enabling retries for such errors ensures temporary network issues do not cause unhandled exceptions. **How** - Modified `integrations/wiz/wiz/client.py` to explicitly pass `extensions={"retryable": True}` in the `http_client.post` call within the `make_graphql_query` method. This enables the retry mechanism provided by the `port_ocean.helpers.retry` module for transient HTTP errors. - Added a new test file, `integrations/wiz/tests/test_client.py`, with a test case (`test_make_graphql_query`) that verifies the `make_graphql_query` method includes `extensions={"retryable": True}` in the HTTP request. The test uses `pytest`, `AsyncMock`, and `MagicMock` to mock the HTTP client and token fetching, ensuring no real API calls are made. - The test confirms that the correct headers, query, variables, and extensions are sent, and that the response data is processed as expected. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][OpsGenie] Include Incidents and Services in resources with offset limit (#1645)
message:
[Integration][OpsGenie] Include Incidents and Services in resources with offset limit (#1645) ## Description What- - Extended the `MAX_OPSGENIE_OFFSET_LIMIT` to apply to incidents and services in addition to alerts, ensuring consistent pagination behavior across these resource types. - Renamed `MAX_OPSGENIE_ALERT_OFFSET_LIMIT` to `MAX_OPSGENIE_OFFSET_LIMIT` to reflect its broader applicability. Why- - The OpsGenie API enforces a limit where the sum of `offset` and `limit` must not exceed 20,000 for paginated requests. Previously, this limit was only applied to alerts, but it also applies to incidents and services although not documented -How- - Added Incident and Services to resource with offset limits ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

All tests should be run against the port production environment(using a testing org).

### Core testing checklist - [ ] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [ ] Resync finishes successfully - [ ] Resync able to create entities - [ ] Resync able to update entities - [ ] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [ ] Scheduled resync able to abort existing resync and start a new one - [ ] Tested with at least 2 integrations from scratch - [ ] Tested with Kafka and Polling event listeners - [ ] Tested deletion of entities that don't pass the selector ### Integration testing checklist - [ ] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [ ] Resync able to create entities - [ ] Resync able to update entities - [ ] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [ ] Resync finishes successfully - [ ] If new resource kind is added or updated in the integration, add example raw data, mapping and expected result to the `examples` folder in the integration directory. - [ ] If resource kind is updated, run the integration with the example data and check if the expected result is achieved - [ ] If new resource kind is added or updated, validate that live-events for that resource are working as expected - [ ] Docs PR link [here](#) ### Preflight checklist - [ ] Handled rate limiting - [ ] Handled pagination - [ ] Implemented the code in async - [ ] Support Multi account ## Screenshots Include screenshots from your environment showing how the resources of the integration will look. ## API Documentation Provide links to the API documentation used for this integration.

subject: [Core] Add support for caching and running kind in a separate process (#1620)
message:
[Core] Add support for caching and running kind in a separate process (#1620) ### **User description** # Description What - Process each kind in a separate process. Save cache to disk/memory. Why - As we can see when we run ocean with limited resources, it cannot even start to process the big amount of data - it gets terminated for OOM. ![ocean_single_process](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9495fbc-4beb-4dc7-933c-bb9f0afad49b) How - Use multiprocessing module and caching. Use cache to save results to disk. We can enable the multiprocessing/cache by setting a flag. Then we Ocean loads and start a resync we can see the we get batches of data until it get terminated for OOM. ![ocean_multi_process_part_1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a80dacb8-9ed1-4ba9-841c-9524e0fdbc9e) We see that the process is terminated for OOM, but the resync continues, it processing the next kind. we can also notice the RAM usage in docker and the drop when the process was terminated. ![ocean_multi_process_part_2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/773955f7-04b6-4e33-909c-f8369280f13d) Notice that even though we had OOM events the resync completed gracefully and didnt delete entities due to the deletion threshold. We can trigger a new resync from the UI and see how it begins. Also we can notice the RAM usage drop in the docker container when a resync is finished and the spike when it begins. ![ocean_multi_process_part_3](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2504450-64ab-4f11-a61b-0443b6f53ca0) ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Opsgenie] Fixed offset tracking in OpsGenie pagination logic (#1699)
message:
[Integration][Opsgenie] Fixed offset tracking in OpsGenie pagination logic (#1699) # Description Previously, get_paginated_resources didn’t track offset, so the max offset limit wasn’t enforced. This change introduces explicit offset tracking to correctly stop pagination at the defined limit. **What** - Fixes an issue in `get_paginated_resources` where the offset limit (`MAX_OPSGENIE_OFFSET_LIMIT`) was not respected due to lack of explicit offset tracking. **Why** - Previously, the client relied solely on the `paging.next` URL returned by the OpsGenie API. While this allowed pagination to work correctly, it made it impossible to enforce an upper bound on the number of items fetched (`MAX_OPSGENIE_OFFSET_LIMIT`)—because we weren’t tracking or checking the effective offset. **How** - - Introduced a `current_offset` counter that increments by `PAGE_SIZE` after each request. - Used this counter to check against the `max_offset_limit` before making the next request. - Adjusted query parameters to only be passed on the first request (subsequent requests use the `paging.next` URL). - Updated tests to reflect and verify correct stop behavior at the offset limit. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Github] Added Support for Pull Request Kind (#1635)
message:
[Integration][Github] Added Support for Pull Request Kind (#1635) # Description What - Added Pull Request resource support to the GitHub V2 integration. This feature allows syncing GitHub pull requests into Port as entities and receiving webhooks for real-time updates. Why - This enhancement provides users with the ability to track and monitor pull requests directly in Port, enabling better visibility into development workflows and metrics like lead time. How - Implemented a PullRequestExporter class to fetch pull request data, added webhook support for real-time pull request events, and included configuration options to select pull requests by state (open, closed, or all). ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

All tests should be run against the port production environment(using a testing org).

### Core testing checklist - [ ] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [ ] Resync finishes successfully - [ ] Resync able to create entities - [ ] Resync able to update entities - [ ] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [ ] Scheduled resync able to abort existing resync and start a new one - [ ] Tested with at least 2 integrations from scratch - [ ] Tested with Kafka and Polling event listeners - [ ] Tested deletion of entities that don't pass the selector ### Integration testing checklist - [ ] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [ ] Resync able to create entities - [ ] Resync able to update entities - [ ] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [ ] Resync finishes successfully - [ ] If new resource kind is added or updated in the integration, add example raw data, mapping and expected result to the `examples` folder in the integration directory. - [ ] If resource kind is updated, run the integration with the example data and check if the expected result is achieved - [ ] If new resource kind is added or updated, validate that live-events for that resource are working as expected - [ ] Docs PR link [here](#) ### Preflight checklist - [ ] Handled rate limiting - [ ] Handled pagination - [ ] Implemented the code in async - [ ] Support Multi account ## Screenshots Include screenshots from your environment showing how the resources of the integration will look. ## API Documentation Provide links to the API documentation used for this integration. GitHub Pull Requests API: - [GitHub Rest Pull Request]( https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls) - [GitHub Rest Pull Request Webhook](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#pull_request) Additional Notes - The pull request resource supports filtering by state (open, closed, all) via the selector configuration - Pull request webhooks provide real-time updates when PRs are opened, edited, closed, or reopened - Added comprehensive tests for both the exporter and webhook processor - Improved API flexibility by allowing separate repo_name and pr_number parameters in get_resource method --------- Co-authored-by: u1b35ebd62876d894

subject: [Integration][Gitlab-V2] Retrieve Jobs from Pipeline Instead of Projects (#1741)
message:
[Integration][Gitlab-V2] Retrieve Jobs from Pipeline Instead of Projects (#1741) # Description What - Changed job fetching to use pipeline context instead of project context to establish proper parent-child relationships between pipelines and jobs Why - The previous implementation fetched jobs directly from projects, which didn't properly represent the hierarchical relationship between pipelines and jobs. This change ensures that jobs are correctly associated with their parent pipelines, providing better data organization and relationship mapping. How - Modified the job fetching logic in gitlab_client.py to: - First fetch pipelines for each project - Then fetch jobs for each pipeline - Yield jobs in batches while maintaining the pipeline context Job fetching is still limited to first page (100 jobs) per **pipeline** (not ~project~ anymore) to prevent excessive data loading ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [X] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Gitlab-v2] Added Support For Ingesting Merge Requests In Different States (#1784) # Description **What** - Added support for filtering merge requests by their state (opened, closed, merged) in the GitLab v2 integration. This enhancement allows users to selectively track merge requests based on their preferred state through a new state selector configuration while still maintain integration performance by only syncing desired states. **Why** - Currently, the integration fetches all merge requests regardless of their state, which can lead to unnecessary data synchronization and potential performance issues. [Integration][Gitlab-V2] Implementation of File Deletion Support in GitLab v2 Integration (#1841) # Description What - - Added support for handling deleted files in GitLab webhook events for the File kind. The implementation properly processes file deletions from push events and reports them to Port's platform. Why - - Previously, the integration was only handling added and modified files, but wasn't properly tracking deleted files. This meant that when files were deleted in GitLab, their state wasn't being accurately reflected in Port. This implementation ensures data consistency between GitLab and Port by properly tracking file deletions. message:
[Integration][bitbucket-cloud] Ensure Files Are Properly Deleted in Port For File Kind Live Events (#1837) # Description What - - Fixes bug in file kind live event where tracked files don't get upserted to port - Fixes a bug in File kind live events where files deleted from the bitbucket-cloud repository were not being properly unregistered (deleted) from Port. The webhook processor now correctly builds a minimal entity for deleted files, ensuring they are removed from Port when deleted in the source repository. Why - - The `get_file_paths` function was failing when `diff_stat.get("old")` or `diff_stat.get("new")` returned `None`, causing `NoneType` object has no attribute `get` exceptions that prevented file processing entirely - Previously, when a file was deleted in bitbucket-cloud, the corresponding entity was not always removed from Port due to incomplete or missing entity construction for deletions. This led to stale file entities persisting in Port, causing data inconsistency and confusion for users tracking file state. How - - Fixed the `get_file_paths` function to handle None values - Refactored the webhook processor’s deletion logic to include all required parameters for entity for deleted files using metadata from the event payload. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][AzureDevOps] Ensure Files Are Properly Deleted in Port For File Kind Live Events (#1833) # Description What - - Fixes a bug in File kind live events where files deleted from the ADO repository were not being properly unregistered (deleted) from Port. The webhook processor now correctly builds a minimal entity for deleted files, ensuring they are removed from Port when deleted in the source repository. Why - - Previously, when a file was deleted in Azure DevOps, the corresponding entity was not always removed from Port due to incomplete or missing entity construction for deletions. [Integration][Jira] Fix JQL Parentheses Handling in Issue Webhook Processor (#1886) ### **User description** # Description What - - Fixes a bug in the Jira integration where user-supplied JQL filters were not properly wrapped in parentheses before appending the issue key condition in the webhook processor. This ensures correct operator precedence and accurate issue fetching during live event processing. Why - - Without proper parentheses, Jira may interpret the combined JQL incorrectly, potentially returning more issues than intended or not filtering for the specific issue key. This could lead to incorrect data being ingested into Port during live events. How - - Updated the webhook processor to wrap user JQL filters in parentheses before appending the `AND key =` ... condition. - Added/updated unit tests to verify correct JQL construction and prevent regressions. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][AWS-v3] add OIDC provider (#1934)
message:
[Integration][AWS-v3] add OIDC provider (#1934) ### **User description** - **feat: add assume role with web identity** - **feat: add vscode debugger profile for AWS v3** - **fix: sts client fails since there's a missing AWS_ROLE_ARN in the env variable of the pod** - **test: the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityProvider class. - Verified the is_refreshable property and successful reading of web identity tokens. - Enhanced credential retrieval logic with mock AWS STS client interactions.** # Description This PR implements a new credential provider `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityProvider` for the AWS v3 integration, enabling authentication using AWS Web Identity tokens. This is particularly useful for Kubernetes (EKS) environments and other federated identity scenarios where applications need to assume AWS roles using OIDC tokens. ### 1. New Credential Provider: `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityProvider` **Location**: `integrations/aws-v3/aws/auth/providers/assume_role_with_web_identity_provider.py` **Key Features**: - Reads web identity token from file specified by `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable - Implements automatic credential refresh using `AioRefreshableCredentials` - Supports optional parameters: `role_session_name`, `duration_seconds`, `provider_id` ### 2. Environment-Based Auto-Detection **Location**: `integrations/aws-v3/aws/auth/session_factory.py` **New Method**: `_detect_provider_type()` **Provider Priority**: 1. **Web Identity** (highest priority): If `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` is set 2. **Assume Role**: If `account_role_arn` is configured This enables seamless integration without configuration changes - the system automatically detects the appropriate authentication method based on environment variables. ## How It Works ### Authentication Flow 1. **Token Reading**: Provider reads web identity token from file specified by `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` 2. **STS Call**: Calls `sts.assume_role_with_web_identity` with token and role ARN ### Basic Usage (Environment Variables) ```bash export AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE="/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token" ``` ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [X] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Core] feat: implement core change for group queue (#1936)
message:
[Core] feat: implement core change for group queue (#1936) ### **User description** # Description Why Problem: GitHub webhook events for the same resource (like a PR) were getting processed out of order when multiple workers ran concurrently. This broke temporal consistency - you'd get a "PR closed" event processed before "PR updated", leading to stale data. Solution: Group events by resource ID and ensure only one worker processes events for any given resource at a time, while still allowing parallel processing across different resources. What Three core changes: Group-based queuing: Added GroupQueue that partitions events by group_id and locks groups during processing Resource identification: Created group_selector.py to extract consistent resource IDs from GitHub webhook payloads Multi-worker coordination: Modified processor manager to spawn multiple workers that respect group locks How Resource Identification: Extract consistent IDs from GitHub events (e.g., pull_request-123, issue-456) to group related events together. Group Queue: Queue implementation that enforces sequential processing within groups while allowing concurrent processing across groups. Workers lock groups on get() and unlock on commit(). Worker Pool: Multiple workers per webhook path, each pulling from the shared group queue. Integration automatically chooses group-aware or simple processing based on worker count configuration. Result: Events for the same resource process in order, different resources process in parallel. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Wiz] Fixed 'NoneType' object is not iterable error when processing service… (#1959)
message:
[Integration][Wiz] Fixed 'NoneType' object is not iterable error when processing service… (#1959) ### **User description** # Description **What** - Fixed a runtime error that caused integration resync to fail when processing Wiz issues that have `null` serviceTickets field instead of an empty array. **Why** - The Wiz API sometimes returns `serviceTickets: null` for issues that don't have any associated service tickets, rather than returning an empty array `serviceTickets: []`. When the integration tried to iterate over these null values during serviceTicket resource processing, Python threw a `'NoneType' object is not iterable` error, causing the entire resync to fail. **How** - Updated the serviceTicket processing logic in `main.py` to handle null values explicitly by changing `issue.get("serviceTickets", [])` to `(issue.get("serviceTickets") or [])`. This ensures that when the API returns `null`, we convert it to an empty list `[]` which can be safely iterated over. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Core] bug fix: transform array form of brokers to the correct brokers list (#1984)
message:
[Core] bug fix: transform array form of brokers to the correct brokers list (#1984) ### **User description** # Description What: Azure integration deployments fail with container crash loops due to broker configuration format mismatch. The Terraform guide specifies Kafka brokers as JSON arrays, but Ocean expects comma-separated strings. Why: The Terraform variables.tf defines brokers as a list of strings, which serializes as JSON arrays in the OCEAN__EVENT_LISTENER environment variable. However, the underlying Kafka client library requires comma-delimited broker addresses. This format incompatibility prevents proper initialization and causes the container to repeatedly crash during startup. How: Implemented a Pydantic validator in KafkaEventListenerSettings that automatically converts JSON array broker strings to comma-separated format. The parse_brokers validator detects bracket-enclosed strings, parses them as JSON arrays, and joins the broker addresses with commas. The solution maintains full backward compatibility by preserving existing comma-separated configurations and gracefully handling malformed JSON inputs. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Integration][AWS-v3] Add organization strategy for multi account (#1995) ### **User description** - **Add OrganizationsStrategy to AWS v3 integration WIP** - **feat: Enhance OrganizationsHealthCheckMixin with role name handling** - **feat: add missing dependency yamllint** - **feat: feat: Enhance session strategy detection and credential handling** - **feat: Add support for AWS Organizations account discovery** # Description ### **Changes Made** #### **1. Enhanced Strategy Detection Logic** - **File**: `integrations/aws-v3/aws/auth/session_factory.py` - **Changes**: - Added `use_organizations` configuration flag support - Implemented comprehensive strategy selection logic: - **OrganizationsStrategy**: When `use_organizations: true` + role ARN(s) provided - **MultiAccountStrategy**: When multiple role ARNs provided (manual configuration) - **SingleAccountStrategy**: When single role ARN or no role ARN provided - Simplified the `create()` method to use the new detection logic - Removed redundant conditional logic and logging #### **2. Added Configuration Option** - **File**: `integrations/aws-v3/.port/spec.yaml` - **Changes**: - Added `useOrganizations` boolean configuration option - Clear description explaining when and how to use the organizations feature - Documented requirement for organization management account role ARN ### 📋 **Configuration Examples** #### **Organizations-based Discovery:** ```yaml accountRoleArn: ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/OrganizationManagementRole"] useOrganizations: true ``` #### **Manual Multi-account (existing behavior):** ```yaml accountRoleArn: - "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ReadRole" - "arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ReadRole" useOrganizations: false # or omit this field ``` #### **Single Account (existing behavior):** ```yaml accountRoleArn: ["arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ReadRole"] # useOrganizations defaults to false ``` ### 🔍 **Technical Details** - **Strategy Priority**: Organizations → Multi-account → Single account - **Role ARN Handling**: Organizations strategy uses the first role ARN as the management account role --- Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [X] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][AWS-v3] convert to use organizations strategy by default (#2071)
message:
[Integration][AWS-v3] convert to use organizations strategy by default (#2071) - **[Integration][AWS-v3] Update AWS Account Role configuration in spec.yaml** - **feat: Enhance AWS Account Role configuration in spec.yaml** - **refactor: Update ResyncStrategyFactory to use account_role_arns** - **feat: Introduce AWSOrganizationsNotInUseError for better error handling** - **fix: Update healthcheck method to use account_role_arns** - **refactor: Improve account role ARN handling in AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityProvider** - **refactor: Revise AWSOrganizationsNotInUseError for clarity** - **refactor: Update account role ARN handling across tests** # Description This PR implements a new organizations-first strategy for the AWS v3 integration that automatically attempts to use AWS Organizations for account discovery, with graceful fallback to single account mode when organizations is not available. This provides a better user experience for most users while maintaining backward compatibility. Previously, users had to manually choose between organizations strategy and single account strategy. This created friction for users who: - Have AWS Organizations enabled but don't know how to configure it - Want to use organizations but fall back gracefully when it's not available - Need to specify exact accounts when organizations isn't an option ### ✨ Solution Implement an intelligent strategy selection system that: 1. **Prioritizes organizations strategy** when a single role ARN is provided 2. **Automatically falls back** to single account mode when organizations is not available 3. **Supports direct multi-account access** for users without organizations ### 🔧 Technical Changes #### 1. Updated Configuration Schema - **Added** `accountRoleArn` (string) for organizations access with fallback - **Added** `accountRoleArns` (array) for direct multi-account access #### 2. Session Factory - **Modified** strategy detection logic to prioritize organizations when single ARN is provided - **Added** support for both configuration formats - **Updated** strategy selection to handle fallback scenarios #### 3. Organizations Strategy - **Added** automatic fallback to single account mode when organizations fails - **Implemented** graceful error handling for organizations-specific failures #### 4. Multi-Account Strategy - **Modified** to use new `accountRoleArns` configuration - **Maintained** existing functionality for direct account access #### 5. Web Identity Provider - **Added** backward compatibility for both configuration formats - **Updated** to handle string and array inputs gracefully #### For Organizations Users (Default Path) ```yaml configurations: - name: accountRoleArn type: string description: "AWS Account Role ARN for organizations access. When provided, the integration will attempt to use AWS Organizations to discover accounts, falling back to single account mode if organizations is not available." ``` #### For Direct Multi-Account Access ```yaml configurations: - name: accountRoleArns type: array description: "Array of AWS Account Role ARNs for direct multi-account access. Use this when you don't have AWS Organizations enabled or want to specify exact accounts to access." ``` --- - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration] [Gitlab-v2] Flexible API Parameters and Configurable access level resource sync (#2072)
message:
[Integration] [Gitlab-v2] Flexible API Parameters and Configurable access level resource sync (#2072) ## What This PR refactors the GitLab integration to replace hardcoded access levels with flexible configuration, enabling better support for self-hosted GitLab instances. The changes include: - Replacing `owned` parameter with flexible `params` in `get_groups()` and `get_parent_groups()` methods - Adding `params` parameter to `get_projects()` and `search_files()` methods for consistency - Introducing `GitlabVisibilityConfig` for runtime access level configuration - Removing hardcoded `DEFAULT_MIN_ACCESS_LEVEL = 30` constant that prevented self-hosted instances from discovering all projects - Updating webhook factory to use explicit `min_access_level: 50` instead of `owned=True` - Adding configuration-driven parameter building throughout all resync functions ## Why The previous approach had several limitations: - **Hardcoded access levels**: `DEFAULT_MIN_ACCESS_LEVEL = 30` prevented self-hosted GitLab instances from discovering all accessible projects - **Limited API flexibility**: `owned` parameter only allowed boolean filtering - **Inconsistent parameter handling**: Different methods used different parameter patterns - **Poor extensibility**: Adding new GitLab API parameters required code changes ## How The refactor introduces flexible parameter passing and configuration-driven access control: ```python # Removed hardcoded constant # DEFAULT_MIN_ACCESS_LEVEL = 30 # ❌ Removed # Flexible API parameters async def get_groups(self, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None) async def get_projects(self, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None) async def search_files(self, params: Optional[dict[str, Any]] = None) # New configuration system class GitlabVisibilityConfig(BaseModel): use_min_access_level: bool = Field(default=True) min_access_level: int = Field(default=30) # Configuration-driven parameter building def _build_visibility_params() -> dict[str, Any]: use_min_access_level, min_access_level = _get_visibility_config() params = {} if use_min_access_level: params["min_access_level"] = min_access_level return params # Consistent parameter merging across all methods request_params = {**self.DEFAULT_PARAMS} if params: request_params.update(params) ``` All resync functions now use `_build_visibility_params()` to apply configurable access control, allowing self-hosted GitLab instances to discover all accessible projects by setting `use_min_access_level: false` in their configuration. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - subject: [Integration][AWS-V2] Add Support For S3 Resource As Standalone Exporter (#1916)
message:
[Integration][AWS-V2] Add Support For S3 Resource As Standalone Exporter (#1916) # Description ## What - Added Support For AWS S3 Exporter This PR introduces a dedicated S3 bucket exporter for the AWS v3 integration, replacing the previous generic CloudControl-based approach with a specialized S3-focused implementation. ## Why - The previous implementation used a generic `cloudResource` blueprint that handled multiple AWS resource types (S3 buckets, EC2 instances, ECS clusters) through AWS CloudControl APIs. This approach had several limitations: 1. **Generic modeling**: All AWS resources were mapped to a single `cloudResource` blueprint, losing S3-specific context and properties 2. **Limited S3 features**: CloudControl APIs don't expose all S3-specific configurations like encryption settings, public access blocks, and detailed bucket properties 3. **Complex configuration**: Users had to work with generic resource mappings and complex JQ expressions rather than intuitive S3-specific field mappings 4. **Performance issues**: Multiple sequential API calls through CloudControl's abstraction layer instead of direct S3 APIs 5. **Reduced functionality**: Missing support for S3-specific actions and detailed bucket metadata ## How - ### 1. New S3-Specific Blueprint - **Replaced**: Generic `cloudResource` and `awsAccount` blueprints - **Added**: Dedicated `s3Bucket` blueprint with S3-specific properties: - `arn`: Amazon Resource Name with proper description - `region`: AWS region location - `creationDate`: Bucket creation timestamp - `encryption`: Bucket encryption configuration object - `publicAccessBlockConfiguration`: Public access block settings - `tags`: Bucket tags array ### 2. Dedicated S3 Exporter Architecture - **New S3BucketExporter class**: Implements `IResourceExporter` interface specifically for S3 buckets - **Action-based data collection**: Modular system with specific actions: - `GetBucketLocationAction`: Retrieves bucket region - `GetBucketArnAction`: Constructs proper S3 ARN - `GetBucketTaggingAction`: Fetches bucket tags (default) - `GetBucketEncryptionAction`: Gets encryption settings (optional) - `GetBucketPublicAccessBlockAction`: Retrieves public access configuration (optional) - `GetBucketOwnershipControlsAction`: Gets ownership controls (optional) ### 3. Flexible Action System - **Default actions**: Always executed (location, ARN, tagging) - **Optional actions**: Configurable via `includeActions` in port-app-config.yml - **ActionMap pattern**: Extensible system for adding new S3 actions ### 4. Enhanced Data Models - **BucketProperties**: Comprehensive S3 bucket property model with 15+ fields - **Bucket**: S3-specific resource model extending base ResourceModel - **Request models**: Separate models for single bucket vs paginated requests ### 5. Improved Configuration & Performance - **Simplified mapping**: Direct S3 property mappings instead of generic resource parsing - **Configurable actions**: Users can specify which S3 actions to include via `includeActions` - **Concurrent processing**: Async batch processing with parallel bucket handling - **Better error handling**: S3-specific error handling for missing permissions and common scenarios ### 6. Testing Coverage - **Comprehensive test suite**: Covering exporter functionality, models, actions, and edge cases - **Isolated unit tests**: Mock-based testing for reliable CI/CD - **Integration scenarios**: Multi-account and region testing ### 7. Updated Integration Flow - **Dedicated resync handler**: `@ocean.on_resync(ObjectKind.S3_BUCKET)` - **Multi-account support**: Works with existing AWS Organizations and role assumption - **Region-aware**: Properly handles S3 global service with region-specific buckets ### 8. Breaking Changes - **Blueprint changes**: Existing `cloudResource` entities will need to be migrated to `s3Bucket` - **Configuration updates**: `useGetResourceAPI` and generic selectors replaced with `includeActions` The new implementation provides a more robust, feature-rich, and maintainable approach to S3 bucket synchronization while maintaining compatibility with existing multi-account and region configurations. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

subject: [Integration][GCP] `gRPC` Fork Deadlock Prevention (#2027)
message:
[Integration][GCP] `gRPC` Fork Deadlock Prevention (#2027) ### **User description** # Description What - Defer real-time quota controller initialization in integrations/gcp/main.py to avoid pre-fork gRPC usage. Why - Multi-process mode uses fork; gRPC (google-cloud clients) is not fork-safe. Initializing gRPC in the parent before forking leads to deadlocks and the warning: “Other threads are currently calling into gRPC, skipping fork() handlers.” How - Replace the on_start call to resolve_request_controllers() with conservative defaults derived from search_all_resources_per_minute_quota (use 80% as effective rate). - No changes to resync/search codepaths; gRPC clients are still instantiated within child execution where it’s safe. - Backward-compatible; behavior remains configurable via integration settings; eliminates fork+gRPC deadlock in multi-process mode. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Gitlab-V2] Added Support For Including Inherited Gitlab Group Members (#2202) ### **User description** # Description What: Added support for including inherited members Why: GitLab groups grant access not only to direct members but also to inherited, shared, and inherited-shared members. Without accounting for these, downstream visibility and access governance are incomplete and can miss users who effectively have access. This change aligns behavior with the GitLab UI and the GitLab Members domain model, improving accuracy of group membership data. How: - Introduced a new selector flag `includeInheritedMembers` (default: false) on `GitlabMemberSelector` for both `group-with-members` and `member` resource kinds in `integrations/gitlab-v2/integration.py`. - Respected the flag in `integrations/gitlab-v2/main.py` within the `GROUP_WITH_MEMBERS` and `MEMBER` resync handlers by propagating it to the GitLab client calls: - `enrich_group_with_members(group, include_bot_members, include_inherited_members)` - `get_group_members(group_id, include_bot_members, include_inherited_members)` - Retrieval uses the GitLab Members API to include indirect members (inherited/shared), consistent with GitLab’s membership model and endpoints (see GitLab docs: [Members overview](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/members/) and [Members API](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/members.html)). - Preserved backward compatibility: behavior is unchanged unless `includeInheritedMembers` is explicitly enabled. - Works in conjunction with existing visibility controls (`useMinAccessLevel`/`minAccessLevel`) and existing bot filtering (`includeBotMembers`). - Maintains current batching and async execution to manage rate limits and performance. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)
