message:
[Integration][AWS-v3] Add ECS Service support to AWS v3 integration (#2191) ### **User description** # Description ## What This PR adds support for AWS ECS Services to the AWS-v3 integration, allowing users to discover and sync ECS services to Port alongside other AWS resources. ## Why ECS Services represent the actual running containerized applications within ECS clusters. The integration already supported ECS Clusters but lacked visibility into the services running within those clusters. Users need to: - Track service configurations and status - Monitor deployment health and task counts - View relationships between services and their parent clusters - Get complete visibility into containerized workloads ## How The implementation follows the existing AWS-v3 patterns: ### Core Components - **Models** (`aws/core/exporters/ecs/service/models.py`): Pydantic models for ECS Service properties including task definitions, deployment configs, and network settings - **Actions** (`aws/core/exporters/ecs/service/actions.py`): `DescribeServicesAction` that fetches service details using the AWS ECS `describe_services` API - **Exporter** (`aws/core/exporters/ecs/service/exporter.py`): `EcsServiceExporter` that discovers services by first listing clusters, then services within each cluster ### Configuration - **Blueprint**: Added `ecsService` blueprint with schema for service properties and relationships - **Port Config**: Resource mappings to transform AWS ECS Service data into Port entities - **Spec**: Added `AWS::ECS::Service` to supported resource kinds ### Testing - Tests for actions and exporter covering various scenarios - Example files with raw AWS data and expected Port output The implementation uses the existing ECS cluster exporter to discover clusters first, then lists and describes services within each cluster to maintain proper parent-child relationships. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

message:
[Integration][Github] Added Support for Multi-Org (#2274) ### **User description** # Description **What** - Added comprehensive multi-organization support to the GitHub Ocean integration **Why** - The current GitHub integration only supports a single organization, limiting its scalability and requiring separate integrations for each organization. This change enables users to manage multiple GitHub organizations through a single integration instance. **How** - - Updated all resync functions to iterate through multiple organizations using organization-specific clients - Modified webhook processors to include organization context in payloads - Enhanced client factory to create organization-specific GitHub clients - Added custom `OrganizationRequiredException` for better error handling - Updated configuration schema to support `githubOrganizations` field - Refactored all resource exporters to work with organization-specific clients ## Type of change - [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) ### Core testing checklist - [x] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [x] Resync finishes successfully - [x] Resync able to create entities - [x] Resync able to update entities - [x] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [x] Scheduled resync able to abort existing resync and start a new one - [x] Tested with at least 2 integrations from scratch - [x] Tested with Kafka and Polling event listeners - [x] Tested deletion of entities that don't pass the selector ### Integration testing checklist - [x] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [x] Completed a full resync from a freshly installed integration and it completed successfully - [x] Resync able to create entities - [x] Resync able to update entities - [x] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [x] Resync finishes successfully - [x] If new resource kind is added or updated in the integration, add example raw data, mapping and expected result to the `examples` folder in the integration directory. - [x] If resource kind is updated, run the integration with the example data and check if the expected result is achieved - [x] If new resource kind is added or updated, validate that live-events for that resource are working as expected - [x] Docs PR link [here](#) ### Preflight checklist - [x] Handled rate limiting - [x] Handled pagination - [x] Implemented the code in async - [x] Support Multi account ## Screenshots Include screenshots from your environment showing how the resources of the integration will look. ## API Documentation Provide links to the API documentation used for this integration. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Tests ___ ### **Description** • Added comprehensive multi-organization support to the GitHub Ocean integration, enabling management of multiple GitHub organizations through a single integration instance • Updated all resync functions and resource exporters to iterate through multiple organizations using organization-specific clients • Enhanced webhook processors to include organization context in payloads and processing logic • Modified configuration schema to support `githubOrganizations` field while making `githubOrganization` optional • Added new `OrganizationRequiredException` for better error handling and organization validation • Updated all core option types to inherit from organization-aware base classes • Refactored utility functions to use `parse_github_options` instead of `extract_repo_params` for organization support • Enhanced file processing, folder mapping, and team management to work with organization-specific contexts • Updated all test suites to include organization parameters and validate multi-organization functionality • Added organization as a new resource kind in the integration specification ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Single Org Config"] --> B["Multi-Org Config"] B --> C["Organization-Specific Clients"] C --> D["Enhanced Resync Functions"] C --> E["Updated Webhook Processors"] C --> F["Modified Resource Exporters"] D --> G["Multi-Org Resource Management"] E --> G F --> G ```

subject: [Integration][AWS] - Fix GeneralServiceException breaking resync on resource not found. (#2287)
message:
[Integration][AWS] - Fix GeneralServiceException breaking resync on resource not found. (#2287) ### **User description** # Description ## What Improved AWS exception handling by enhancing `is_resource_not_found_exception()` and `is_access_denied_exception() `to correctly detect cases where AWS CloudControl API returns `GeneralServiceException` wrapping underlying errors such as `ResourceNotFoundException` or `AccessDenied.` ## Why The AWS CloudControl API, which the integration sometimes uses to fetch and manage resource states, sometimes returns a top-level error code of GeneralServiceException even when the underlying issue is more specific — such as ResourceNotFoundException or AccessDenied. In these cases, CloudControl wraps the actual downstream service error (for example, from EC2 or S3) inside the GeneralServiceException message string instead of exposing it as a structured error code. As a result, our existing helper functions — is_resource_not_found_exception() and is_access_denied_exception() — failed to recognize these conditions because they only checked the top-level error code. This led to legitimate “not found” or “permission denied” cases being treated as unhandled exceptions, which interrupted the entire resync process rather than skipping the problematic resource and continuing graceful **Example of the problematic error:** ``` Error Code: "GeneralServiceException" Message: "The Vpc Endpoint Id 'vpce-068e7950f9d5142c6' does not exist" ``` ## How - Enhanced `is_resource_not_found_exception()` to check for `GeneralServiceException` and inspect the error message for resource not found patterns: "not found", "notfound", "does not exist", "resourcenotfound" - Enhanced `is_access_denied_exception()` to check for `GeneralServiceException` and inspect the error message for access denied patterns: "access denied", "accessdenied", "unauthorized", "forbidden", "permission denied" - Made pattern matching case-insensitive using `.lower()` - Added comprehensive tests to validate the new behavior - Maintained backward compatibility - all existing error codes continue to work as before **Result:** Resources with wrapped errors are now logged and skipped gracefully instead of breaking the resync, allowing the integration to continue processing remaining resources. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Core] Fixed JSON serialization error caused by Decimal data types (#2345)
message:
[Core] Fixed JSON serialization error caused by Decimal data types (#2345) # Description **What** - Fixed JSON serialization error caused by Decimal data types in GitLab v2 GitOps integration **Why** - When `yield_items_to_parse` is enabled, `ijson.items_coro()` returns Decimal objects for numeric values, which are not JSON-serializable. subject: [Integration][Github] Use Search API for Repo Export With GitHub App Auth (#2455)
message:
[Integration][Github] Use Search API for Repo Export With GitHub App Auth (#2455) ### **User description** …hub app # Description What - - Use the GitHub Search API for repository export when authenticated as a GitHub App, or when explicit search_params are provided. - Add default qualifiers when search_params are not provided (include forks and scope by repository type). Refactor repository export into _list_strategy and _search_strategy for clarity and maintainability. Why - - Ensure correct and consistent repository discovery for GitHub App installations. - Improve behavior by aligning results with visibility/type and including forks where appropriate. - Make the logic easier to extend and reason about. How - - Introduced GitHubAppAuthenticator check to select strategy. - Built search query with sensible defaults when explicit search parameters are absent. - Preserved previous list API flow for non-App contexts. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior)

All tests should be run against the port production environment(using a testing org).

### Core testing checklist - [x] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [x] Resync finishes successfully - [x] Resync able to create entities - [x] Resync able to update entities - [x] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [x] Scheduled resync able to abort existing resync and start a new one - [x] Tested with at least 2 integrations from scratch - [x] Tested with Kafka and Polling event listeners - [x] Tested deletion of entities that don't pass the selector ### Integration testing checklist - [x] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [x] Completed a full resync from a freshly installed integration and it completed successfully - [x] If resource kind is updated, run the integration with the example data and check if the expected result is achieved - [x] If new resource kind is added or updated, validate that live-events for that resource are working as expected - [ ] Docs PR link [here](#) ### Preflight checklist - [ ] Handled rate limiting - [ ] Handled pagination - [ ] Implemented the code in async - [ ] Support Multi account ## Screenshots Include screenshots from your environment showing how the resources of the integration will look. ## API Documentation Provide links to the API documentation used for this integration. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Bug fix ___ ### **Description** - Refactor repository export to use Search API for GitHub App authentication - Add default qualifiers (fork:true, repository type) when search parameters absent - Split export logic into _list_strategy and _search_strategy for maintainability - [Integration][Github] - Add Labels Selector to GitHub Issue Kind (#2513) ### **User description** # Description ## What Adds a new `labels` field to the `GithubIssueSelector` class that allows filtering GitHub issues based on labels during both webhook processing and resync operations. Issues must have **ALL** of the specified labels (AND logic) to be ingested. ## Why This enhancement provides users with more granular control over which GitHub issues are ingested into Port. Previously, users could only filter issues by state (open/closed/all) and repository query, but couldn't filter based on specific labels. This is particularly useful for: - Ingesting only issues with certain labels like "bug", "enhancement", or "priority:high" - Creating focused dashboards for specific issue categories - Reducing noise by filtering out issues that don't match organizational workflows - Supporting label-based triage and categorization processes ## How ### Configuration Changes - Added `labels: Optional[str]` field to `GithubIssueSelector` with description and example usage - Updated `ListIssueOptions` to include the optional `labels` parameter ### Filtering Logic Implementation - Created `issue_matches_labels()` utility function in `github/helpers/utils.py` that: - Accepts issue labels list and comma-separated required labels string - Uses AND logic (all required labels must be present) - Handles empty/null inputs gracefully ### Webhook Processing - Modified `IssueWebhookProcessor.handle_event()` to check labels filter before processing - Added early return with empty results when labels don't match - Integrated filtering check before existing state-based logic ### Resync Integration - Updated `main.py` resync_issues function to pass `labels` parameter to issue listing operations ### Testing - Added unit tests in `test_issue_webhook_processor.py` covering: - Exact label matches (all required labels present) - Partial matches (missing some labels) - No labels specified (default behavior) - Edge cases with empty strings ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

[Integration][Github] Add GraphQL Pull Request Exporter (#2528) ### **User description** # Description What - - Introduce a GraphQLPullRequestExporter for GitHub pull requests using the GraphQL API. - Add an includeExtraFields/includeExtraFields selector on the GitHub pull request kind to opt into richer PR data. - Wire the GraphQL exporter into pull request resync and webhook processing, falling back to the existing REST exporter by default. - Extract common PR updated-at filtering logic into a shared utility. - Add a dedicated webhook processor for GitHub ping events and register it in the webhook registry. Why - - We want to expose richer, structured pull request metadata (assignees, requested reviewers, counts, additional fields) without complicating the existing REST exporter or breaking current users. - Using GraphQL for PRs when explicitly enabled allows us to fetch all needed fields in a single, well-shaped query while keeping the default behavior and performance characteristics of the existing REST flow. - Handling ping webhook events explicitly avoids unnecessary noise, makes webhook health checks explicit, and keeps logs and processing paths clear. message:
[Integration][AWS] - Refresh account list on resync instead of startup (#2523) ### **User description** # Description Fix AWS Account Refresh on Resync ### **What** Move AWS account discovery from integration startup to resync operations to ensure account changes are immediately reflected. **Before:** Accounts were discovered once on startup and cached indefinitely **After:** Accounts are refreshed before each resync cycle ### **Why** Fixes PORT-16916 where the AWS integration would not refresh the account list on resync operations. When accounts are added to or removed from AWS Organizations, the integration continued using stale account data from the initial startup discovery, causing: - New accounts to be missed during resync - Removed accounts to still appear in results - Account metadata changes (names, status) to not be reflected ### **How** **Code Changes:** - **Removed** `await initialize_access_credentials()` from `@ocean.on_start()` handler - **Added** new `@ocean.on_resync_start()` handler that calls `initialize_access_credentials()` before each resync cycle **Technical Details:** - `initialize_access_credentials()` triggers `SessionManager.reset()` which rediscovers all accounts from AWS Organizations API - The `@ocean.on_resync_start()` hook runs once per resync cycle, before all resource resync operations - All resync functions (including account resync) now use freshly discovered account data ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][Custom] add dependency to spec (#2507) # Description This document describes the dependency relationships defined in `spec.yaml` for the Ocean Custom Integration. These dependencies are **UI-only metadata** that control field visibility and required state in Port's installation UI. ## Purpose The dependency system allows us to: - **Improve UX**: Show only relevant fields based on user selections ## Important Notes for Reviewers ⚠️ **These dependencies are purely for UI display purposes and do NOT affect integration logic.** - The integration code uses `config.get()` with sensible defaults, so missing fields won't break functionality - All fields remain optional at the code level - dependencies only control UI visibility - This is a **suggestion** for better UX - reviewers should be pragmatic about whether dependencies are necessary or helpful ## Dependency Structure ### Authentication Dependencies Fields are conditionally shown based on the selected `authType`: | Field | Visible When | Required When | |-------|-------------|---------------| | `apiToken` | `authType == "bearer_token"` | `authType == "bearer_token"` | | `username` | `authType == "basic"` | `authType == "basic"` | | `password` | `authType == "basic"` | `authType == "basic"` | | `apiKey` | `authType == "api_key"` | `authType == "api_key"` | | `apiKeyHeader` | `authType == "api_key"` | Never (has default) | **Example**: When a user selects `authType: "bearer_token"`, only the `apiToken` field becomes visible and required. Other auth fields are hidden. ### Pagination Dependencies Fields are conditionally shown based on the selected `paginationType`: | Field | Visible When | Required When | |-------|-------------|---------------| | `pageSize` | `paginationType in ["offset", "page", "cursor"]` | Never (has default) | | `paginationParam` | `paginationType in ["offset", "page", "cursor"]` | Never (has defaults) | | `sizeParam` | `paginationType in ["offset", "page", "cursor"]` | Never (has defaults) | | `startPage` | `paginationType == "page"` | Never (has default) | | `cursorPath` | `paginationType == "cursor"` | Never (has defaults) | | `hasMorePath` | `paginationType in ["offset", "page", "cursor"]` | Never (has defaults) | **Example**: When a user selects `paginationType: "cursor"`, fields like `cursorPath`, `pageSize`, `paginationParam`, `sizeParam`, and `hasMorePath` become visible. Fields specific to other pagination types (like `startPage` for page-based) remain hidden. ## Implementation Details ### YAML Structure Each field with dependencies follows this pattern: ```yaml - name: fieldName required: false # Base requirement (always false for optional fields) type: string description: "..." dependencies: - on: dependentField when: equals: "value" # or "in: [value1, value2]" then: visible: true required: true # or false if field has defaults ``` ### Why Fields Are Not Required Most pagination fields are marked as `required: false` even when visible because: 1. The integration code provides sensible defaults (e.g., `pagination_param` defaults to "offset", "page", or "cursor" based on type) 2. Users may not need to customize these values for standard API patterns 3. Making them optional reduces friction while still providing visibility when needed ## Benefits 1. **Cleaner UI**: Users only see fields relevant to their configuration 2. **Better guidance**: Required fields are clearly indicated when applicable 3. **Reduced errors**: Less chance of users filling in wrong fields 4. **Maintainability**: Dependencies are declarative and easy to update ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [X] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Core] Add Base Config Change Webhook Processor (#2610)
message:
[Core] Add Base Config Change Webhook Processor (#2610) ### **User description** # Description What - - Introduce a `BaseConfigChangeWebhookProcessor` base class for config change webhooks. - Mark config change processors as `ACTION` processors and provide a standard `trigger_resync` interface that triggers a full resync via `ocean.sync_raw_all()`. subject: [Integration][AWS-v3] Refactor AWS-v3 authentication to execute at resync start (#2584)
message:
[Integration][AWS-v3] Refactor AWS-v3 authentication to execute at resync start (#2584) # Description ## What Refactor AWS-v3 authentication to add session lifecycle management via Ocean hooks and standardize error handling. This includes: - Moving authentication initialization to `@ocean.on_resync_start()` hook for predictable timing - Adding `@ocean.on_resync_complete()` hook to clear AWS account sessions for memory management - Standardizing all strategies to raise exceptions instead of returning `False` for consistent error handling - Simplifying `get_account_sessions()` by removing redundant checks after `healthcheck()` calls - Reducing log noise by removing redundant log messages ## Why 1. **Multi-process Efficiency**: In multi-process execution mode, each resource kind runs in a separate subprocess. Without initialization in the main process via `@ocean.on_resync_start()`, each subprocess would independently recreate the strategy and run healthcheck, causing redundant work and wasted resources. Moving initialization to the hook ensures it happens once in the main process before subprocesses are spawned. 2. **Memory Management**: Sessions were persisting in memory between resyncs, causing memory accumulation. The strategy object and all its state (ARNs, sessions, discovered accounts) need to be cleared after each resync to ensure proper garbage collection. 3. **Consistency**: Strategies had inconsistent error handling - `MultiAccountStrategy` and `OrganizationsStrategy` returned `False` on some failures while `SingleAccountStrategy` always raised exceptions, making error handling unpredictable. 4. **Code Quality**: Redundant checks after `healthcheck()` calls violated DRY principles. Since `healthcheck()` now always raises on failure, these checks are unnecessary. ## How 1. **Added session lifecycle management**: - Created `initialize_aws_account_sessions()` function that creates strategy and calls `healthcheck()` - Hooked into `@ocean.on_resync_start()` to ensure authentication happens before any kind processing - Created `clear_aws_account_sessions()` function that sets `AccountStrategyFactory._cached_strategy = None` - Hooked into `@ocean.on_resync_complete()` to clear the strategy after resync completes, making all ARNs, sessions, and state eligible for garbage collection 2. **Standardized error handling**: - `MultiAccountStrategy.healthcheck()` now raises `AWSSessionError` instead of returning `False` when no ARNs provided - `OrganizationsStrategy.healthcheck()` now raises `AWSSessionError` instead of returning `False` when no accounts discovered - All strategies now have uniform fail-fast behavior 3. **Simplified `get_account_sessions()` methods**: - Removed redundant success checks after `healthcheck()` calls in `MultiAccountStrategy` and `OrganizationsStrategy` - Since `healthcheck()` now always raises on failure, no need to check return values - Moved session None check in `SingleAccountStrategy` to after account_id check for better error message ordering 4. **Code cleanup**: - Removed redundant log messages in `resync.py` that were misleading or duplicated information - Updated log messages for clarity (e.g., "Starting account discovery" → "Starting resync") 5. **Updated tests**: - Modified tests to expect exceptions instead of `False` returns - Added test for `clear_aws_account_sessions()` to verify strategy and state are cleared ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

[Integration][Checkmarx-one] - Fix token expiration recalculation bug in Checkmarx integration (#2579) ### **User description** ## Description What - Fixed a bug where token expiration time was incorrectly recalculated when loading tokens from cache, causing tokens to appear to never expire. Why - When loading a cached token, the code used `time.time() + expires_in` instead of `cached_at + expires_in`, which extended the expiration each time the token was loaded. This could lead to using expired tokens and authentication failures. How - - Changed `_get_access_token()` to use `cached_at` from the cached token data instead of `time.time()` when calculating expiration - Added test cases to verify correct expiration calculation from cache - Added test to ensure expiration doesn't extend on multiple cache loads ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Core] Fix RetryTransport Sleep for Epoch Based Rate-limit Headers (#2689)

[Core] Fix RetryTransport Sleep for Epoch Based Rate-limit Headers (#2689) ### **User description** # Description What - - Improve RetryTransport retry delay calculation by reading retry-related response headers and correctly interpreting large numeric retry values as UNIX epoch timestamps. Why - Some APIs return rate-limit reset headers (or retry headers) as epoch timestamps; treating them as “seconds to wait” can cause extremely long sleeps or incorrect retry behavior. How - - Update _parse_retry_header() to detect large numeric values and convert epoch reset times into a sleep duration. - Pass the previous response headers into _calculate_sleep() so configured retry-after headers can be respected. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][GitHub] Retry Rate-limit 403 Responses with Reset-aware Backoff (#2690) ### **User description** # Description What - - Added GitHubRetryTransport to retry GitHub 403 responses that include rate-limit exhaustion headers. - Increased GitHub retry backoff window and centralized the “rate limit headers exhausted” predicate. - Updated GitHub rate limiter/client tests to match the current behavior. message:
[CI][core-release-workflow] - auto create tag and release on push to main (#2625) # Description This PR automates the Ocean framework release workflow by automatically creating tags and GitHub releases when the version in `pyproject.toml` changes on the `main` branch. ### Changes #### 1. **Automatic Tagging** (`tag-main` job) - Triggers on push to `main` when `pyproject.toml` changes - Compares current version with previous commit's version - Automatically creates and pushes tag `v{version}` when versions differ - Uses explicit tag ref (`refs/tags/v{version}`) to ensure proper tag push #### 2. **Automatic GitHub Release** (`create-release` job) - Creates GitHub release automatically after tag is created - Uses GitHub's auto-generated release notes based on commits - Marks as pre-release if version contains `-` (e.g., `1.2.3-beta`) - Only runs when version changes #### 3. **PyPI Publishing** (`publish_ocean` job) - Now depends on `tag-main` job completion - Checks out the created tag before building and publishing - Only runs when version changes (prevents duplicate publishes) - Maintains existing PyPI publish and Slack notification functionality ### Benefits - ✅ **No manual tagging required** - tags are created automatically when version changes - ✅ **Automatic release notes** - GitHub generates release notes from commits - ✅ **Consistent workflow** - ensures tag → release → PyPI publish sequence - ✅ **Manual dispatch support** - workflow can still be triggered manually via `workflow_dispatch` ### Workflow Flow 1. Developer bumps version in `pyproject.toml` and merges to `main` 2. `tag-main` detects version change → creates tag `v{version}` 3. `create-release` creates GitHub release with auto-generated notes 4. `publish_ocean` publishes to PyPI and sends Slack notification ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Custom] add custom authentication method (#2667)
message:
[Integration][Custom] add custom authentication method (#2667) # Custom Authentication for HTTP Server Integration This PR adds support for **custom authentication methods** to the `@integrations/custom` integration, enabling OAuth2, JWT, and other dynamic token-based authentication flows beyond the standard types (Bearer, Basic, API Key). ## Overview When `authType` is set to `"custom"`, you configure: 1. **How to authenticate** (`customAuthRequest`) - defines the auth endpoint, method, headers, and body 2. **How to use the token** (`customAuthResponse`) - defines where to inject auth values in subsequent requests using template syntax The integration automatically: - Authenticates on startup - Caches evaluated templates for performance - Refreshes tokens proactively (if `reauthenticateIntervalSeconds` is configured) or reactively on 401 errors - Handles concurrent requests safely with locking ## Configuration ### `customAuthRequest` (Required) Defines how to make the authentication request: | Field | Type | Description | Example | |-------|------|-------------|---------| | `endpoint` | string | Auth endpoint (relative path or full URL) | `"/oauth/token"` or `"https://auth.example.com/token"` | | `method` | string | HTTP method (default: `"POST"`) | `"POST"`, `"GET"` | | `headers` | object | HTTP headers for auth request | `{"Content-Type": "application/json"}` | | `body` | object | JSON request body (mutually exclusive with `bodyForm`) | `{"grant_type": "client_credentials"}` | | `bodyForm` | string | Form-encoded body (mutually exclusive with `body`) | `"grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=..."` | | `queryParams` | object | Query parameters | `{"scope": "read"}` | | `reauthenticateIntervalSeconds` | integer | Token validity duration in seconds. If not provided, tokens only refresh on 401 errors. A 60-second buffer refreshes proactively before expiration. | `3600` | ### `customAuthResponse` (Required) Defines how to use the authentication response in subsequent API requests using template syntax `{{.jq_path}}`: | Field | Type | Description | Example | |-------|------|-------------|---------| | `headers` | object | Headers to add/override with template values | `{"Authorization": "Bearer {{.access_token}}"}` | | `queryParams` | object | Query params to add/override with template values | `{"api_key": "{{.access_token}}"}` | | `body` | object | Body fields to add/override with template values | `{"token": "{{.accessToken}}"}` | **Template Syntax:** Use `{{.jq_path}}` to extract values from the auth response. Supports nested paths like `{{.data.token}}` or `{{.nested.field.value}}`. **Note:** At least one of `headers`, `queryParams`, or `body` must be provided. ## Examples ### OAuth2 Client Credentials Flow ```yaml authType: "custom" customAuthRequest: endpoint: "/oauth/token" method: "POST" headers: Content-Type: "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" bodyForm: "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=${CLIENT_ID}&client_secret=${CLIENT_SECRET}" reauthenticateIntervalSeconds: 3600 # Refresh every hour customAuthResponse: headers: Authorization: "Bearer {{.access_token}}" ``` ### API Key in Query Parameter ```yaml authType: "custom" customAuthRequest: endpoint: "/api/auth/login" method: "POST" headers: Content-Type: "application/json" body: username: "${USERNAME}" password: "${PASSWORD}" customAuthResponse: queryParams: api_key: "{{.apiKey}}" ``` ### Token in Multiple Places ```yaml authType: "custom" customAuthRequest: endpoint: "/v1/auth/token" method: "POST" body: clientId: "${CLIENT_ID}" clientSecret: "${CLIENT_SECRET}" customAuthResponse: headers: Authorization: "Bearer {{.access_token}}" X-API-Version: "{{.version}}" queryParams: token: "{{.access_token}}" body: auth_token: "{{.access_token}}" ``` ## How It Works 1. **Startup**: Integration authenticates once using `customAuthRequest` configuration 2. **Template Evaluation**: Values from auth response are extracted using JQ paths (e.g., `{{.access_token}}`) 3. **Request Injection**: Evaluated templates are injected into headers, query params, or body for each API request 4. **Token Refresh**: - **Proactive**: If `reauthenticateIntervalSeconds` is set, tokens refresh 60 seconds before expiration - **Reactive**: On 401 errors, tokens automatically refresh and the request retries 5. **Caching**: Evaluated templates are cached until auth response changes, improving performance ## Migration - **No Breaking Changes**: Existing auth types (`bearer_token`, `basic`, `api_key`, `none`) continue to work - **New Feature**: Custom auth is opt-in - set `authType: "custom"` to use it ## Technical Details - Template syntax is validated at configuration time (fail-fast) - Thread-safe re-authentication prevents concurrent refresh attempts - Shared client singleton ensures consistent auth state across all requests - Supports environment variable substitution in config values (e.g., `${CLIENT_ID}`) ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [Core] feat: adjust Dockerfile use unprivileged user (#2432) ### **User description** # Description What Refactored the Docker image and startup scripts to transition the Ocean user to a strictly non-privileged account (UID 1001) without sudo access. Implemented a user-space mechanism for handling CA certificates. Why Many enterprise security policies (e.g., strict Kubernetes clusters, OpenShift) prohibit containers running with root privileges or users with sudo access. The previous implementation required sudo to run update-ca-certificates when new certs were mounted, which blocked deployment in these secure environments. How Removed Privileges: Removed the sudo package and the specific sudoers configuration that allowed the ocean user to run root commands. User-Space Cert Sync: Introduced sync_ca_certs.sh, a script that: Scans system and mounted certificate directories (e.g., /etc/ssl/certs). Copies them to a user-owned directory (/home/ocean/.local/share/ca-certificates). Generates a local ca-certificates.crt bundle. Environment Configuration: Configured standard SSL environment variables (SSL_CERT_DIR, SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE) to force applications (Python, curl, etc.) to use the new user-owned certificate location instead of the system default. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Integration][Pagerduty] - Increase PagerDuty Rate Limit Threshold to Prevent 429 Errors (#2683) ### **User description** # Fix: Increase PagerDuty Rate Limit Threshold to Prevent 429 Errors ## Description ### What - Increased the proactive rate limit threshold from `1` to `15` in the PagerDuty rate limiter - Improved error handling in `send_api_request` by explicitly initializing the response variable - Updated and added tests to verify the new threshold behavior ### Why - The previous threshold of `1` was too aggressive, causing the integration to continue making requests until the absolute limit was reached - With `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS = 10`, multiple concurrent requests could all proceed when `remaining > 1`, leading to rate limit violations (429 errors) before the limiter could pause - PagerDuty enforces a strict rate limit of 960 requests per minute, and with large datasets (e.g., 10,000 incidents requiring 100+ API requests), the integration was frequently hitting this limit - The old error handling pattern using `if "response" in locals()` was less readable and maintainable ### How - Changed `_proactive_remaining_threshold` from `1` to `15` in `PagerDutyRateLimiter.__init__()` to provide a safety buffer for concurrent requests - Updated `send_api_request` to explicitly initialize `response: httpx.Response | None = None` and capture `response = e.response` in the exception handler - Replaced `if "response" in locals()` with `if response:` for cleaner, more Pythonic code - Updated `test_enters_pause_when_remaining_le_threshold` to test the new threshold value of 15 - Added `test_does_not_pause_when_remaining_above_threshold` to verify requests proceed when remaining > 15 ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

[Integration][Jenkins] Prevent Resync Mapping Timeouts by Caching Iterator Chunks (#2718) ### **User description** # Description What - Updated the Jenkins integration to use cache_iterator_result() for get_jobs()/get_builds() so cache hits replay paginated chunks (instead of yielding one large flattened list), and added a Jenkins changelog entry. Why - Large Jenkins instances (e.g., ~13k jobs) can produce a single massive batch on cache-hit, causing Ocean’s entity parsing/mapping to exceed per-item timeouts and fail resync with ExceptionGroup(... message:
[Integration][SonarQube] Fix Pagination Reset in SonarQube Issues Ingestion (#2744) ### **User description** # Description What: During resync, the SonarQube integration fails to ingest issues for projects after processing one with >10,000 issues. The shared query_params dict retains a high "p" (page) value from the previous project, causing subsequent fetches to start from an invalid page (e.g., 101), resulting in empty responses despite existing issues. Why: This leads to incomplete or zero-issue ingestion for multi-project setups, causing data loss in Port Ocean. Resetting pagination ensures independent, full fetches per project, adhering to SonarQube's 10k result cap without state carryover. How: In integrations/sonarqube/client.py's `get_issues_by_component`: - Create a deep copy of query_params using copy.deepcopy. - Set project-specific "components" or "componentKeys" on the copy. - Remove any existing "p" key with .pop("p", None) to reset to page 1. - Pass the isolated copy to _send_paginated_request. This isolates mutations per project without altering the original dict. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Bitbucket-server] Resolved `Future attached to a different loop` error in bitbucket-server multiprocess resync (#2762)
message:
[Integration][Bitbucket-server] Resolved `Future attached to a different loop` error in bitbucket-server multiprocess resync (#2762) ### **User description** # Description What - Fixed the bitbucket-server integration crashing with `Future attached to a different loop` when syncing large numbers of pull requests Why - In multiprocess mode, Ocean forks a subprocess per resource kind. The forked subprocess creates a new asyncio event loop via `asyncio.run()`, but the cached `BitbucketClient` singleton (inherited from the parent via fork) holds an `aiolimiter.AsyncLimiter` whose internal futures are bound to the parent's event loop. When the rate limiter's capacity is exhausted (~104 PRs in the reported case), `acquire()` awaits a future tied to the old loop, causing the crash. How - Added a PID check to `init_client()` so that after a fork the client is recreated with a fresh `AsyncLimiter` bound to the new event loop. The previous limiter's consumption state (`_level` and `_last_check`) is carried over to the new instance so the rate limit budget is preserved across resource kinds. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

message:
[Integration][Argocd] Stop accumulation of cluster resources (#2774) ### **User description** # Description What - This stops the accumulation of resources in `get_resources_for_available_clusters` client method. Argocd does not support pagination, we should advise customers to enable streaming if they have a large environment; trade-offs between sync time and memory use can be made by configuring the chunk_size and the buffer size, by default this is set to 64KB chunk size and 64MB buffer size, these are good defaults imo, so the only configuration requirement in most cases would be to enable streaming: `OCEAN__STREAMING__ENABLED=true` Why - While this improves memory slightly when streaming is disabled, it more than doubles sync time to do it. But most consequentially, it completely negates any advantage we get from enabling streaming (see attached spreadsheet). How - Rather than accumulate all streamed items, buffer up to specified page size. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ x ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior)

subject: [Integration][Jira] Fix webhook search index lag causing missed issue creation (PORT-17308) (#2765)
message:
[Integration][Jira] Fix webhook search index lag causing missed issue creation (PORT-17308) (#2765) # Description What - Webhook processor now uses `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with `reconcileIssues` parameter instead of `GET` when verifying newly created/updated issues against JQL filters. Why - Jira's search index is eventually consistent. When a `jira:issue_created` webhook arrives, the integration re-queries the Search API with the configured JQL filter, but ~20% of the time the issue isn't indexed yet. The issue doesn't pass the JQL filter and is incorrectly marked for deletion instead of creation. Issues only appear after the next resync (3min–8 hours). Zendesk #6713 / #5259. How - Added `search_issues_by_ids()` method to `JiraClient` that uses `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` with a JSON body containing `reconcileIssues` — a Jira API parameter that guarantees read-after-write consistency for specified issue IDs. The webhook processor now extracts `issue.id` from the payload and calls this method instead of `get_paginated_issues()`. The resync path (`get_paginated_issues` via GET) is completely untouched. ## Diagram Walkthrough ### Before (bug) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Jira participant Webhook as Webhook Processor participant Search as Jira Search API (GET) participant Port Jira->>Webhook: jira:issue_created {key: TEST-1, id: 12345} Webhook->>Search: GET /search/jql?jql=(project=TEST) AND key=TEST-1 Note over Search: Search index hasn't
caught up yet Search-->>Webhook: {issues: []} (empty — not indexed) Webhook->>Port: Mark TEST-1 for DELETION ❌ Note over Port: Issue missing until
next resync (3min–8hrs) ``` ### After (fix) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Jira participant Webhook as Webhook Processor participant Search as Jira Search API (POST) participant Port Jira->>Webhook: jira:issue_created {key: TEST-1, id: 12345} Webhook->>Search: POST /search/jql {jql: "...", reconcileIssues: [12345]} Note over Search: reconcileIssues guarantees
read-after-write consistency Search-->>Webhook: {issues: [{key: TEST-1, ...}]} ✅ Webhook->>Port: Upsert TEST-1 ✅ Note over Port: Issue appears immediately ``` ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ### Integration testing checklist - [x] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [x] Completed a full resync from a freshly installed integration and it completed successfully - [x] Resync able to create entities - [x] Resync able to update entities - [x] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [x] Resync finishes successfully - [x] If new resource kind is added or updated in the integration, add example raw data, mapping and expected result to the `examples` folder in the integration directory. - [x] If resource kind is updated, run the integration with the example data and check if the expected result is achieved - [x] If new resource kind is added or updated, validate that live-events for that resource are working as expected - [ ] Docs PR link [here](#) ### Preflight checklist - [x] Handled rate limiting - [x] Handled pagination - [x] Implemented the code in async - [x] Support Multi account ## File Walkthrough | File | Change | Diff | |------|--------|------| | `integrations/jira/jira/client.py` | Add `search_issues_by_ids()` — POST-based search with `reconcileIssues` for read-after-write consistency | +19/-0 | | `integrations/jira/webhook_processors/issue_webhook_processor.py` | Extract `issue.id` from payload, call `search_issues_by_ids` instead of `get_paginated_issues` | +9/-10 | | `integrations/jira/tests/test_client.py` | Add 2 tests for `search_issues_by_ids` (success + empty response) | +50/-0 | | `integrations/jira/tests/test_processors.py` | Update all issue webhook tests to use `search_issues_by_ids` with `AsyncMock`; [Core] Port-app-config schema propagation (#2766) ### **User description** # Description - Added new `ocean port-app-config schema` and `ocean port-app-config list-kinds` CLI commands that let consumers extract the PortAppConfig JSON schema and enumerate the resource kinds defined by any integration, without running the integration itself. - Enriched `PortAppConfig` and `ResourceConfig` model fields with titles, descriptions, and UI-schema metadata so the generated schema is self-documenting. - Introduced `kind_validators.py` which enforces schema validation rules at class-definition and query time: - **No duplicate `Literal` kind values** -- if two `ResourceConfig` subclasses declare the same `Literal["..."]` kind, a `TypeError` is raised. - **At most one custom-kind slot** -- only a single `ResourceConfig` with `kind: str` (the catch-all / custom-kind) is allowed; [Core][CI] Upload Port-app-config schemas in release workflow (#2794) ### **User description** # Description ## Upload port-app-config schemas to S3 ### Summary - Restructure the S3 schema storage layout so integration spec and port-app-config schemas live in versioned folders (`//`). - Generate **port-app-config** and **port-app-config UI** schemas at release time by running the integration Docker image with `ocean port-app-config schema` (default and `-f ui`). - Maintain backward compatibility by continuing to write the legacy `.json` file at the bucket root for the integration service. ### Motivation Until now, only the integration spec was uploaded to S3. To support schema-driven UI and validation, we now also publish the **port-app-config** JSON schema and its **UI variant** (dereferenced selectors) for each integration version. ### S3 layout change **Before:** ``` / ├── index.json ├── github-ocean.json (latest spec) └── github-ocean/ ├── github-ocean-1.0.0.json (versioned spec) ├── github-ocean-2.0.0.json (versioned spec) └── ... ``` **After:** ``` / ├── index.json ├── github-ocean.json (legacy latest spec — kept for integration service) └── github-ocean/ ├── 3.0.0/ │ ├── spec.json │ ├── port_app_config.json │ └── port_app_config.ui.json ├── 3.1.0/ │ ├── spec.json │ ├── port_app_config.json │ └── port_app_config.ui.json ├── spec.json (latest) ├── port_app_config.json (latest) ├── port_app_config.ui.json (latest) └── ... ``` ### What changed - **`release-integrations.yml`** — Refactored the S3 upload step to: 1. Upload `spec.json` to a versioned folder (`//spec.json`) instead of the flat `/-.json` layout. 2. Upload latest `spec.json` at `/spec.json` and keep writing the legacy `.json` at the root. 3. Run the released Docker image to generate `port_app_config.json` (default schema) and `port_app_config.ui.json` (UI format via `ocean port-app-config schema -f ui`). 4. Upload both schemas to the versioned folder and, when it’s the new latest release, also under `/`. 5. Gracefully skip schema upload if Docker generation fails (log a warning). ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [X] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Integration][Custom] File-based endpoint response cache for custom integration resync (#2803) ### **User description** # Description What - File-based streaming cache for API endpoint responses that are reused across multiple resource kinds during a single resync in the custom (HTTP server) integration. Why - In dynamic configurations, the same API endpoint (e.g., `/api/v2/tickets.json`) can be fetched multiple times: once per duplicate kind mapping and again during path parameter resolution for dependent kinds (e.g., comments). This causes redundant API calls, wasted time, and unnecessary rate limit consumption. How - - Added `EndpointCache` class that pre-analyzes all resource configs at resync start to identify endpoints used 2+ times (both as direct kinds and as `path_parameters` discovery endpoints). - Only those endpoints are cached — single-use endpoints pass through with zero overhead. - Raw paginated responses are written as NDJSON lines to temp files (write-through), then streamed back line-by-line on cache hits, keeping memory usage constant regardless of data size. - Cache is initialized via `@ocean.on_resync_start()` and cleaned up via `@ocean.on_resync_complete()`. - Cache key normalization ensures `None` vs `{}` and method casing differences produce the same key across call sites (`fetch_endpoint_data` vs `query_api_for_parameters`). ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][GCP] Bounded project concurrency and fixed gRPC fork safety (#2792)
message:
[Integration][GCP] Bounded project concurrency and fixed gRPC fork safety (#2792) # Description What - Fixes resource overload, SSL corruption, and SIGSEGV crashes in the GCP integration during resync. Why - Unbounded concurrency in `iterate_per_available_project` launched all projects simultaneously, exhausting memory and gRPC channels. Ocean's fork-based processing then inherited broken gRPC state, causing SSLV3_ALERT_BAD_RECORD_MAC / TSI_DATA_CORRUPTED / SIGSEGV (-11). How - Replaced per-call gRPC client instantiation with lazy-init singletons (gcp_core/clients.py), reducing channel churn. - Bounded project concurrency in `iterate_per_available_project` using `semaphore_async_iterator`. - Added `os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=...)` to reset client singletons after fork, preventing children from reusing or finalizing inherited gRPC channels. Inherited objects are parked in an orphaned list to avoid GC triggering TLS writes on shared sockets. - Registered clients.close on the signal handler to properly await transport shutdown. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Integration][GitHub] Fix includedFiles Relative Resolution for Monorepos (#2815) ### **User description** # Description What - - Refactors GitHub includedFiles enrichment into a dedicated module and updates resync + webhook flows to use it. - Fixes includedFiles path resolution so folder/file kinds resolve relative to each matched folder/file (monorepo-safe) and avoids base-path double-joins. - Adds/updates tests for relative resolution, resolver edge cases, repo/branch matching, and fetcher caching/in-flight dedup. subject: [Integration][Azure-DevOps] Handle manual test runs without build field in code (#2804)
message:
[Integration][Azure-DevOps] Handle manual test runs without build field in code (#2804) What - Fixed KeyError crash when syncing test runs that lack a 'build' field Manual test runs (created via Test Plans UI/API) now sync successfully with empty code coverage Why - When `codeCoverage` selector is enabled for `test-run` kind, the integration crashes with: KeyError: 'build' This happens because: 1. Code coverage is fetched using the build ID from each test run 2. **Manual test runs** (created via Test Plans, not pipelines) don't have a `build` field 3. The code assumed all test runs come from pipeline builds How - Added check before accessing `build.id`: ```python self._fetch_code_coverage(project_id, run["build"]["id"], coverage_config) if run.get("build") and run["build"].get("id") else self._no_coverage() ``` Runs without builds get __codeCoverage: {} instead of crashing. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

[Integration][Bitbucket Server] Fix projectFilterRegex selector not being applied during resync (#2829) ### **User description** # Description **What** - Fixed a bug where the `projectFilterRegex` selector value was never actually applied when filtering projects, repositories, and pull requests during resync. The regex was being read from the event context at client-initialisation time and stored on the client instance, but the client is a singleton — so the regex was always `None` for any resync that did not happen to initialise the client. **Why** - The `projectFilterRegex` field on the selector is a per-resource-config value. Reading it once at client-init time (from `event.resource_config`) is incorrect because the client is shared across all resource kinds and all resync cycles. The value must be read from the selector at call time and passed directly into the filtering methods. **How** - Removed `project_filter_regex` from the client constructor and config, and instead pass it directly from the selector into `get_projects`, `get_repositories`, and `get_pull_requests` at call time in each resync handler. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Github] Fixed rate limiter race conditions and restore page size (#2833)
message:
[Integration][Github] Fixed rate limiter race conditions and restore page size (#2833) ### **User description** # Description What - Fixed two race conditions in GitHubRateLimiter and restored the REST pagination page size to 100. Why - The previous implementation read `x-ratelimit-remaining` from every response and used it as the source of truth. Because the server snapshot does not account for in-flight requests from the same process, concurrent coroutines all saw the same stale remaining value and could pile through simultaneously. Additionally, writing on every response created a feedback loop of conflicting state. How - - `GitHubRateLimiter` now initialises its state (limit, remaining, reset_time) from the first response per window only. Subsequent normal responses are ignored — on_response returns early when `_initialized` is `True`. - Each slot granted in `__aenter__` decrements remaining optimistically under the lock, so concurrent coroutines always see a strictly decreasing counter. - State is reset (`_initialized` = `False`) automatically when the epoch `reset_time` passes or after sleeping through an exhausted window, triggering a fresh server read at the start of the next window. - `429/403` exhaustion responses force-update state including retry-after header support, then block further requests until the reset time. - on_response now takes the full `httpx.Response` so all classification logic stays inside the limiter (zero rate-limit logic in the client). - Restored `PAGE_SIZE` to 100 in `rest_client.py`. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

All tests should be run against the port production environment(using a testing org).

subject: [Integration][Github] Added support for retry transient server errors (500/502) for GraphQL POST requests (#2845)
message:
[Integration][Github] Added support for retry transient server errors (500/502) for GraphQL POST requests (#2845) ### **User description** # Description What - Adds retry support for transient server errors (`500 Internal Server Error`, `502 Bad Gateway`) on GitHub GraphQL API requests, and refactors how retry configuration is declared per client type. Why - GraphQL requests use `POST`, which is excluded from the default retryable methods (since REST `POST` mutations are not idempotent). However, GraphQL `POST` requests are always reads and are safe to retry. Without this fix, a transient `502` on `POST /graphql` crashes the entire resync rather than recovering automatically. How - - Added `_extra_retryable_methods: frozenset` as a class attribute on `AbstractGithubClient` (defaults to `frozenset()`). Subclasses override it to declare any HTTP methods they need retried beyond the defaults. - `GithubGraphQLClient` overrides it with `frozenset({"POST"})` — the only client that sends retryable POST requests. - `AbstractGitHubAuthenticator.get_client(extra_retryable_methods)` now accepts extra methods, unions them with the standard defaults (`HEAD`, `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`), and caches one `httpx.AsyncClient` per unique configuration. This means exactly two clients are ever created: one for REST, one for GraphQL. - Added `500` to `additional_retry_status_codes` (GitHub-wide) and added both `500` and `502` to `ignore_retry_after_status_codes` so transient server errors use exponential backoff instead of waiting on rate-limit headers. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][GitHub] Updated GraphQL states variable to include merged pull requests  (#2849)
message:
[Integration][GitHub] Updated GraphQL states variable to include merged pull requests (#2849) ### **User description** # Description An inconsistency exists in Ocean’s GitHub Pull Request ingestion logic between the REST and GraphQL implementations. The REST API client correctly retrieves all closed pull requests. In GitHub’s data model, closed pull requests include both: • Pull requests that were closed without merge • Pull requests that were successfully merged However, the GraphQL client does not return merged pull requests when requesting closed pull requests. The issue stems from the status variable used in the GraphQL query. The query does not explicitly include merged pull requests in its filter criteria before execution. As a result: • REST client behavior: • closed → returns both closed (unmerged) and merged pull requests (correct behavior) • GraphQL client behavior: • closed → returns only closed-unmerged pull requests • Merged pull requests are excluded from the response This leads to incomplete ingestion when using the GraphQL client, causing discrepancies in data between integrations depending on which client is used. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

[Core] make caching decorators concurrency safe (#2850) ### **User description** # Description What - Make ocean caching decorators concurrency safe, this prevents cache-misses caused by race condition. Why - At the moment, when concurrent requests are launched and try to access a cache, if the cache is empty they'll all bypass the cache and make a request to the source api, then all update the cache. How - Add lock before writing to the cache. Use weakvaluedict so locks will be dropped after the last holder has exited. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][Gitlab-v2] Fall back to project-level file search when groups are inaccessible (#2801)
message:
[Integration][Gitlab-v2] Fall back to project-level file search when groups are inaccessible (#2801) ### **User description** # Description What - Adds a fallback to project-level file search in `on_resync_files()` when the group-level search returns no results. Why - When a token has project-level access only (e.g. a service account added to individual projects), `get_parent_groups()` returns empty, causing `kind: file` to yield 0 results. Other resource kinds (`project`, `merge-request`) work correctly with the same token. This is also a regression from gitlab v1, which used project-level search. How - Added `search_files_in_projects()` to `GitLabClient` that iterates all accessible projects and searches each via `GET /projects/{id}/search`. In `on_resync_files()`, if the existing group-level search yields nothing (and no specific repos are configured), the handler falls back to this project-level search. subject: [Integration][AWS] Implement safe region check for AWS resource during resync (#2862)
message:
[Integration][AWS] Implement safe region check for AWS resource during resync (#2862) ## Description Region-level errors during AWS resync (e.g., `TypeNotFoundException` when a resource type isn't registered in a region) were preventing the reconciliation delete phase from running, causing stale entities to accumulate in Port. ## What - Added `is_resource_type_not_available_exception()` classifier to distinguish benign region errors from real failures - Updated `_handle_global_resource_resync()` to log and try the next region on any error instead of raising immediately - Updated `resync_resources_for_account()` to only raise `ExceptionGroup` for real errors, not benign ones ## Why `resync_resources_for_account()` raised an `ExceptionGroup` for any region failure. Ocean core converted this to `OceanAbortException`, causing `_resync_reconciliation()` to skip the delete phase entirely. Since not every resource type is available in every AWS region, benign errors like `TypeNotFoundException` consistently blocked reconciliation — leading to stale entities accumulating (~200k instead of ~5k). ## How Errors are now classified into two categories: | Category | Error codes | Behavior | |----------|------------|----------| | **Benign** | `TypeNotFoundException`, `CFNRegistryException`, `UnsupportedActionException`, `AccessDeniedException` | Logged and suppressed — reconciliation runs normally | | **Real** | Everything else (`InternalServiceError`, `ThrottlingException`, network errors, etc.) | Collected and raised as `ExceptionGroup` — reconciliation correctly skips the delete phase | ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Core] feat: add webhook events lakehouse (#2896)
message:
[Core] feat: add webhook events lakehouse (#2896) # Description # Webhook Events to Lakehouse Integration ## What Adds an interceptor that sends webhook event raw data to the lakehouse API with operation metadata (UPSERT/DELETE), mirroring the existing resync flow. ## Why The lakehouse needs a complete audit trail of all raw data received from webhooks, similar to how resync events are tracked. This enables: - Data replay/recovery from raw webhook events - Audit trail of what data arrived via webhooks - Consistent lakehouse data collection across sync and webhook flows ## How ### 1. Created `LakehouseOperation` enum ```python class LakehouseOperation(StrEnum): UPSERT = "UPSERT" DELETE = "DELETE" ``` ### 2. Updated lakehouse API to accept operation ```json { "items": [/* raw data */], "extractionTimestamp": 1234567890000, "operation": "UPSERT" } ``` ### 3. Added interceptor in webhook flow ```python async def sync_raw_results(self, webhook_events_raw_result): # Send raw data to lakehouse BEFORE transformation await self._send_webhook_raw_data_to_lakehouse(webhook_events_raw_result) # Then parse and apply to Port entities_to_create, entities_to_delete = await self._parse_raw_event_results_to_entities(...) ... ``` ### 4. Flow diagram ``` Webhook → Process → Send Raw to Lakehouse → Parse → Apply to Port (with operation type) ``` ## Example **GitHub repository webhook arrives:** ```json { "action": "edited", "repository": {"id": 123, "name": "my-repo"} } ``` **Webhook processor enriches it:** ```python # Webhook has minimal data, fetch full repository data_to_upsert = await exporter.get_resource(options) # Returns: {"id": 123, "name": "my-repo", "stars": 100, "language": "Python", ...} ``` **Interceptor sends to lakehouse:** ```http POST /lakehouse/.../sync/webhook-event-456/kind/repository/items ``` ```json { "items": [{"id": 123, "name": "my-repo", "stars": 100, "language": "Python", ...}], "operation": "UPSERT", "extractionTimestamp": 1234567890000 } ``` **Then parsed and sent to Port** for entity creation. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

If `false` (Default), continues to hit the legacy metrics API. subject: [Core] add integration test infra (#2853)
message:
[Core] add integration test infra (#2853) # Integration Testing Framework ## What This PR Adds A new **integration testing framework** that lets you test full resync pipelines end-to-end without making real network calls. It mocks both third-party APIs and Port API at the HTTP transport layer, running everything in-process. ## The Problem It Solves Currently, testing integrations requires: - Setting up real API credentials - Making actual HTTP calls (slow, flaky, rate-limited) - Complex mocking that doesn't cover the full pipeline - Manual verification of entity transformations This makes it hard to: - Test edge cases and error scenarios - Verify JQ transformations work correctly - Ensure backward compatibility after changes - Catch bugs before they hit production ## How It Works (Simplified) 1. **Subclass `BaseIntegrationTest`** and define: - Mock routes for third-party APIs (`create_third_party_transport()`) - Port mapping configuration (`create_mapping_config()`) - Integration config (`create_integration_config()`) 2. **The framework handles the rest:** - Boots your integration in-process - Intercepts all HTTP calls (both third-party and Port) - Runs the full resync pipeline: `@ocean.on_resync` → JQ transformation → Port upsert - Returns captured entities and errors 3. **Write assertions** on the results: ```python async def test_resync_creates_entities(self, resync: ResyncResult): assert len(resync.upserted_entities) > 0 assert len(resync.errors) == 0 ``` ## What Gets Tested ✅ **Full resync pipeline** - from `@ocean.on_resync` handlers to Port upserts ✅ **JQ transformations** - entity mappings, selectors, relations (full JQ processing pipeline is exercised) ✅ **Error handling** - exceptions are captured and returned ✅ **Entity deletions** - reconciliation phase with deletion tracking ✅ **Port API interactions** - auth, blueprint fetching, entity upserts/deletes ## What Doesn't Get Tested ❌ **`@ocean.on_start()` handlers** - initialization logic isn't exercised ❌ **Integrations using custom HTTP clients** - only works with integrations that use: - `port_ocean.utils.async_http.http_async_client` (recommended) - `port_ocean.helpers.async_client.OceanAsyncClient` (also supported) Integrations that create their own `httpx.AsyncClient` instances or use `requests` may not be fully covered ❌ **Parallel execution** - tests must run serially due to global state ## Technical Details - **Location**: `port_ocean/integration_testing/` - **HTTP interception**: Patches `httpx` transport layer, no network calls - **Port API mocking**: Pre-configured `PortMockResponder` handles all Port endpoints - **Test isolation**: Resets Ocean singleton and HTTP client state between tests ## Example Usage See `integrations/fake-integration/integration_tests/test_integration_resync.py` for a complete example. ## Running Tests ```bash # From an integration directory make test/integration ``` ## Files Changed - **New**: `port_ocean/integration_testing/` - framework code - **Updated**: `integrations/fake-integration/integration_tests/` - example tests - **Updated**: `integrations/_infra/Makefile` - test command ## Review Focus Areas 1. **HTTP patching mechanism** (`harness.py:_patch_http_clients`) - subject: [Integration][ArgoCD] Improved cluster resource fetch throughput with semaphore-controlled concurrency (#2927)
message:
[Integration][ArgoCD] Improved cluster resource fetch throughput with semaphore-controlled concurrency (#2927) # Description - Introduces a semaphore to control concurrent resource fetch operations per cluster in the ArgoCD integration. - Optimizes throughput of resource retrieval while preventing excessive parallelism and reducing contention on the ArgoCD API. What - Introduce bounded, semaphore-controlled concurrency for fetching ArgoCD resources per available cluster, using `MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_CLUSTER_REQUESTS` to limit in-flight cluster queries. Why - Unbounded or loosely controlled concurrency when calling get_paginated_resources per cluster can overload the ArgoCD API, increase latency under load, and cause throttling when many clusters are present. How – In get_resources_for_available_clusters, we: - Retrieve all available cluster names and construct the resource URL for the given resource_kind. - Create an asyncio.Semaphore configured with MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_CLUSTER_REQUESTS. - Wrap each per-cluster get_paginated_resources call in semaphore_async_iterator, ensuring only a fixed number of cluster queries run concurrently. - Use stream_async_iterators_tasks(*tasks) to asynchronously stream and yield batched resource lists as the throttled tasks complete. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][GitHub] Added pre-computation of `__is_default_branch` during branch entity hydration (#2962) # Description What - Pre-compute __is_default_branch as a native boolean field on branch entities during hydration, eliminating the need for an expensive JQ computed property. Why - Customers using `.name == .__repository_object.default_branch` in their branch kind mapping experienced ingestion times increasing from ~3 hours to ~8 hours. The JQ engine converts the entire raw item dict (including the large __repository_object with 100+ fields) into its internal representation for every property evaluation on every branch entity. Called in both get_resource() and _hydrate_branch() so single-fetch and paginated paths are covered. Customers can now map ` .__ is_default_branch` (a direct field access) instead of the JQ comparison. subject: [Integration][Jira] Add Jira Versions (Releases) as a new synced resource kind (#2799)
message:
[Integration][Jira] Add Jira Versions (Releases) as a new synced resource kind (#2799) ### **User description** ## Description **What** - Adds Jira Versions (Releases) as a new synced resource kind (`version`) in the Jira Ocean integration, surfacing them as first-class entities in the Port catalog. **Why** - Jira Versions (Releases) are a core planning and delivery concept in Jira. Teams use them to track which issues are targeted for a release and monitor release progress. Without this, Port users had no way to catalog or query their Jira releases. **How** - - Added `VERSION` to the `Kinds` enum - Added `get_paginated_versions()` to `JiraClient` — iterates over all projects and yields version batches, enriching each with `__projectKey` so the project relation resolves correctly - Added `get_single_version()` to `JiraClient` — fetches a single version by ID and resolves `__projectKey` via an extra project lookup (the `/rest/api/3/version/{id}` endpoint only returns `projectId` as an integer, not the key string) - Registered 9 `jira:version_*` webhook events and implemented `VersionWebhookProcessor` for real-time updates - Added `jiraVersion` blueprint and port-app-config mapping with properties: `url`, `released`, `archived`, `startDate`, `releaseDate`, `description` and a `project` relation ## Type of change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ### Integration testing checklist - [ ] Integration able to create all default resources from scratch - [ ] Completed a full resync from a freshly installed integration and it completed successfully - [ ] Resync able to create entities - [ ] Resync able to update entities - [ ] Resync able to detect and delete entities - [ ] Resync finishes successfully - [x] New resource kind added — example blueprint and mapping included in `.port/resources/` - [ ] Validate that live-events for `version` are working as expected - [ ] Docs PR link [[here](https://claude.ai/claude-code-desktop/local_77ab8756-7ded-4f80-9490-2fb440103d07#)](#) ### Preflight checklist - [x] Handled pagination (project-level pagination via `_get_paginated_data`;
