subject: [Integration][Checkmarx] Added HTTP 502/503 to ignorable transient errors to prevent resync abortion (#3007)
message:
[Integration][Checkmarx] Added HTTP 502/503 to ignorable transient errors to prevent resync abortion (#3007)

# Description

**What**: HTTP 502 (Bad Gateway) and 503 (Service Unavailable) responses
from the Checkmarx API are now classified as ignorable transient errors
in `CheckmarxOneClient._DEFAULT_IGNORED_ERRORS`.

**Why**: During a scheduled resync, transient 502/503 responses from the
Checkmarx API were propagating as unhandled exceptions out of the ETL
loop in Ocean core's `sync_raw_all()`. When an exception escapes this
loop, the reconciliation phase (`_resync_reconciliation`) is bypassed
and `_handle_resync_abortion()` is called instead. This means stale
vulnerability entities that have been remediated in Checkmarx are never
deleted from Port until a resync completes entirely without any
transient errors.

**How**: Added `IgnoredError` entries for status codes 502 and 503 to
`_DEFAULT_IGNORED_ERRORS` in `checkmarx_one/clients/client.py`. The
`RetryTransport` already retries both codes up to 10 times with
exponential backoff at the transport layer. After retries are exhausted,
`_should_ignore_error()` now matches 502/503, logs a warning, and
returns `{}` rather than re-raising. `send_paginated_request` receives
`{}`, resolves `items` to `[]`, and exits cleanly via the `if not items:
break` guard — allowing the ETL loop and reconciliation to complete
normally.

subject: [Integration][Github-Copilot] - parse NDJSON from Copilot signed URLs  (#2949)
message:
[Integration][Github-Copilot] - parse NDJSON from Copilot signed URLs (#2949) # Description What Fix parsing of Copilot usage metrics reports fetched from GitHub signed URLs. Why GitHub returns signed URL responses as NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), meaning the response contains multiple JSON objects separated by newlines. The previous implementation used `response.json()`, which expects a single JSON document. When multiple objects are present it raises `JSONDecodeError: Extra data` on the second line, causing only the first record to be processed while the remaining report chunks were ignored for organizations with more than one segment. How Replace `response.json()` with line-by-line parsing. The response text is split on newline characters, blank lines are filtered out, and each line is parsed individually using `json.loads()`. This correctly supports both single-object responses (smaller organizations) and multi-object NDJSON responses (larger organizations). Tests cover both formats and use real `httpx.Response` objects instead of mocks so the parsing logic is exercised end-to-end. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][Jira] Switch issue search from GET to POST and unify reconcile search (#2977)
message:
[Integration][Jira] Switch issue search from GET to POST and unify reconcile search (#2977) # Description What - Switched get_paginated_issues from GET to POST on /rest/api/3/search/jql - Removed get_reconciled_issues — merged into get_paginated_issues via reconcileIssues param - Extracted _build_issue_search_body to own all POST body construction Why GET requests encode JQL as a query parameter, which breaks for complex or long JQL queries that exceed URL length limits. POST sends the JQL in the request body, which is Atlassian's recommended approach. Unifying the two search methods removes duplication — both were hitting the same endpoint with the same body shape, differing only by reconcileIssues. How - _build_issue_search_body builds the POST body: converts fields to array, passes expand as string, sets maxResults to len(reconcileIssues) or PAGE_SIZE - _get_paginated_data_using_next_page_token POSTs and threads nextPageToken via immutable body spread - Webhook processor now calls get_paginated_issues with reconcileIssues: [issue_id] instead of the removed get_reconciled_issues ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][Jira] Fix OAuth sync abort on 401 (#3045)
message:
[Integration][Jira] Fix OAuth sync abort on 401 (#3045) # Description What - Marked only the JQL search POST request as retryable by passing `retryable=True` via `extensions` in `_send_api_request`, and updated existing tests to reflect this. Why - Jira issue sync uses `POST` to the JQL search endpoint (`/rest/api/3/search/jql`). The ocean retry transport excludes `POST` from retryable methods by default, so when an OAuth token expires mid-sync, the 401 response bypasses the retry loop entirely, `refresh_request_auth_creds` is never called and the ocean core raises `OceanAbortException`, aborting the full sync. How - Added a `retryable` parameter to `_send_api_request` (default to `False`) and set it to `True` only in `_get_paginated_data_using_next_page_token`. No changes to `JiraRetryTransport` or ocean core defaults. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Why - - Prevent mapping/transformation failures like Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable when integrations (e.g. YAML parsing) introduce Python-native date/datetime values into raw payloads. Improve reliability across all integrations without requiring per-integration workarounds. How - - Introduced port_ocean/core/utils/json_compat.py with make_json_compatible(...). - Added tests in port_ocean/tests/core/utils/test_json_compat.py. subject: [Core] Fix Retry Transport For Incomplete Chunked Reads (#3033)
message:
[Core] Fix Retry Transport For Incomplete Chunked Reads (#3033) # Description What - Fix Ocean core retry behavior so transient httpx.RemoteProtocolError during response body reads (e.g. “incomplete chunked read”) doesn’t abort resync when the response is chunked/unknown-length. Why - Some APIs (e.g. GitHub) can close a chunked response mid-stream, raising during body reads outside the retry loop, which causes resync to fail even though the request should be retryable. How - - Prefetch chunked/unknown-length response bodies inside the retry loop so body-read failures are retried. - Make response-size logging resilient (best-effort) so monitoring doesn’t break request execution. - Add a unit test that simulates a chunked body read raising RemoteProtocolError and asserts the transport retries and succeeds. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][Azure] Fix Literal kind definitions and enable custom kinds for schema validation compliance (#2954)
message:
[Integration][Azure] Fix Literal kind definitions and enable custom kinds for schema validation compliance (#2954) # Description What - Added explicit kind definitions for known Azure resource kinds, added dedicated resource config models per kind, enabled `allow_custom_kinds = True` on `AzurePortAppConfig` to support arbitrary Azure resource kinds, and added `title` and `description` fields to all selector fields. Why - Ocean framework requires explicit `Literal` kinds for schema extraction and the Mapping UI. Azure's `AzureSpecificKindsResourceConfig` needs `kind: str` to support arbitrary Azure resource kinds defined by users; so `allow_custom_kinds = True` is the correct opt-in approach here. subject: [Integration][Jira] refactor: update token on the client when hit 401 (#3114)
message:
[Integration][Jira] refactor: update token on the client when hit 401 (#3114) # Description What - Refactor the Jira client to store the refreshed token for requests to use. Why - After a token rotation occurs, we observe multiple 401 Unauthorized responses on the first attempt across concurrent requests. This happens because the refreshed token is only applied within the retry logic, rather than being set as the default authentication token for all subsequent requests. In contrast, the gitlab-v2 integration handles this more effectively by updating the token at the client level. Why - Users need visibility into who has access to each GitLab project, including inherited members from parent groups. This was requested in the [Port roadmap](https://roadmap.port.io/ideas/p/support-for-inherited-group-members-and-projects-members-including-inherited-in). subject: Enable Support For Fetching AWS Resources From Target OUs (#3145)
message:
Enable Support For Fetching AWS Resources From Target OUs (#3145) # Description What - Added an optional organizationUnitId configuration parameter to the AWS-v3 integration that allows users to scope account discovery to a specific AWS Organization Unit (OU) rather than the entire organization. Why - In large AWS organizations, users may only want to manage resources within a specific OU (e.g., a business unit or environment boundary). Without this, the integration would always attempt to discover and sync every account across the full organization, which may include accounts the user doesn't own or care about. How - Added organizationUnitId as an optional config field in spec.yaml When an organizationUnitId is provided, the integration narrows its account discovery to only that OU instead of scanning the entire organization. It does this by starting at the specified OU, collecting all active accounts directly under it, then walking down through any child OUs and collecting their accounts too — recursively, until the full subtree has been covered. If no OU ID is provided, the integration falls back to its original behavior of discovering all accounts across the whole organization. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] New Integration (non-breaking change which adds a new integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Non-breaking change (fix of existing functionality that will not change current behavior) - [ ] Documentation (added/updated documentation)

subject: [Integration][PagerDuty] Handled daily rate limits for `analytics` endpoints (#3175)
message:
[Integration][PagerDuty] Handled daily rate limits for `analytics` endpoints (#3175) - Added support for respecting PagerDuty's `daily-ratelimit-*` headers on analytics endpoints, preventing excessive 429 errors and dropped enrichment. - Introduced `PagerDutyDailyRateLimitExceededError` to manage daily quota exhaustion. - Enhanced logging for skipped analytics enrichment due to rate limit issues. - Updated version to 0.5.50 in `pyproject.toml` and documented changes in `CHANGELOG.md`. - Added tests to ensure correct behavior under rate limit conditions. # Description What - Teach the PagerDuty integration to honor the analytics-only daily-ratelimit-* headers so resyncs stop hammering 429s once the daily quota is exhausted. Why - Analytics endpoints (/analytics/metrics/..., /analytics/raw/...) enforce a separate, much smaller daily quota (e.g. 10/day) than the per-minute one (~960/min). The current rate limiter only parses ratelimit-* headers, so it never noticed daily exhaustion. Worse, OceanAsyncClient's default retry transport silently retries 429s using ratelimit-reset (~56s), burning ~10 attempts × ~56s ≈ 9 minutes per call before our code even sees the failure — and every concurrent in-flight analytics call enters the same doomed loop. Net effect: long resyncs, dropped analytics enrichment, no clear signal in logs. How - Extended `RateLimiterRequiredHeaders` with the three `daily-ratelimit-*` aliases and added `daily_rate_limit_info` tracking on `PagerDutyRateLimiter`. Daily state is updated only when those headers are present so REST responses don't clobber it. - Added PagerDutyRateLimiter.check_daily_budget(endpoint) and a PagerDutyDailyRateLimitExceededError. send_api_request calls it before acquiring the semaphore so subsequent analytics calls short-circuit without HTTP. - Introduced PagerDutyRetryTransport(RetryTransport) (wired via OceanAsyncClient(transport_class=...)). It feeds the limiter from every response (including intermediate 429s) via after_retry_async, and overrides _should_retry_async to return False for any 429 with daily-ratelimit-remaining ≤ 0 — so the very first daily-quota 429 surfaces in seconds and concurrent retry loops also bail out on their next iteration. - main.py catches PagerDutyDailyRateLimitExceededError narrowly in service and incident analytics enrichment paths, logs at WARNING, and returns un-enriched entities with __analytics: None instead of erroring. - Added unit tests for the new headers, check_daily_budget, the transport hooks, and the end-to-end retry loop short-circuit. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][AWS-V3] Allow Custom Control of AWS Credential Priority Order For authentication (#2424) ### **User description** # Description **What** Refactored the AWS `AccountStrategyFactory` to support **dynamic credential provider priority configuration**. Instead of a hard-coded provider detection order, the factory now reads provider priority from an environment variable (`PROVIDER_PRIORITY`) and selects the first applicable credential provider at runtime. **Why** Previously, `_detect_provider_type()` was statically defined to always prefer `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityProvider`, then `StaticCredentialProvider`, and finally `AssumeRoleProvider`. This made it impossible for clients to customize the order of provider resolution, which limited flexibility in multi-account and mixed-auth scenarios (e.g., when web identity or static credentials should take precedence depending on the environment). **How** * Introduced a provider factory registry mapping provider names to their classes. * Added `_get_provider_priority()` method to read and parse the `PROVIDER_PRIORITY` environment variable (e.g., `PROVIDER_PRIORITY="static,assume_role_with_web_identity,assume_role"`). * Retained existing fallback behavior (`AssumeRoleProvider`) to ensure backward compatibility. * Added clear log statements for visibility into provider selection. ## Type of change * [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) --- Would you like me to include a short **example usage snippet** and **environment configuration example** at the bottom (as some teams do for context in PRs)? subject: [Integration][Github Copilot] Fix HTTP 413 Payload Too Large on user-usage-metrics resync for large GitHub organizations (#3177)
message:
[Integration][Github Copilot] Fix HTTP 413 Payload Too Large on user-usage-metrics resync for large GitHub organizations (#3177) # Description What - Why - For large GitHub organizations (e.g. ~1.4k+ MAU), the Copilot usage metrics endpoints return NDJSON files with tens of thousands of rows (~15k rows, ~59MB). The integration was parsing the full NDJSON and yielding all records in a single Ocean yield. Ocean then POSTed the entire batch to the lakehouse raw ingest endpoint, which responded with HTTP 413 `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE` before the transform phase could begin. The same oversized batch also caused high memory pressure during JQ transform with potential OOM. How - Updated tests to verify chunking behaviour covering: - Large payloads split into correct number of fixed-size batches - No data loss across batches - Enrichment (`__organization` / `__enterprise`) present on every record in every batch - Empty reports yield nothing - Reports without `day_totals` yield nothing - Multiple organizations each yield separate chunked batches ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

subject: [Integration][Claude] Add timeFrame selector to claude-code-analytics for per-day backfill (#3192)
message:
[Integration][Claude] Add timeFrame selector to claude-code-analytics for per-day backfill (#3192)

## Summary

- Added `timeFrame` selector field to `claude-code-analytics` — accepts
an integer number of days to look back from today; the integration calls
the Anthropic Claude Code analytics API **once per day** for each day in
the window
- `timeFrame` and `startingDate` are **mutually exclusive** — exactly
one must be provided (enforced by a Pydantic model validator).
`startingDate` iterates from the given date to today, one API call per
day
- This design matches the API's per-day response structure (each record
carries a `.date` field, unlike usage/cost which are time-bucketed
ranges)
- Usage and cost selectors are unchanged — they remain range-based with
a required `startingDate`
- Default mapping uses `timeFrame: 30` (last 30 days)

## Test plan
- [ ] Deploy with `timeFrame: 30` — verify 30 API calls are made and
data lands for each day
- [ ] Deploy with `timeFrame: 1` — verify only today's data is fetched
- [ ] Deploy with `startingDate: '2026-01-01'` — verify iteration from
that date to today
- [ ] Confirm providing both `timeFrame` and `startingDate` raises a
validation error
- [ ] Confirm providing neither raises a validation error
- [ ] Confirm usage and cost kinds are unaffected

subject: [Core] Whitelist `SentinelOne` and `Anthropic` in IP blocker trusted subdomains to fix hostname rewriting for hosted custom integrations (#3172)
message:
[Core] Whitelist `SentinelOne` and `Anthropic` in IP blocker trusted subdomains to fix hostname rewriting for hosted custom integrations (#3172) # Description What - Custom Ocean integrations hosted by Port (SaaS) connecting to SentinelOne and Anthropic endpoints fail with consistent 401 errors. Port's SSRF protection layer resolves hostname to its raw IP and rewrites the outbound request URL, breaking the domains' SNI/hostname-based routing since the API gateway cannot match the request to the correct tenant without the hostname in the TLS handshake. Why - Customer confirmed the token and base URL are correct; manual API calls to the correct hostname succeed with the same credentials. How - Added `.sentinelone.net` and `api.anthropic.com` to `_TRUSTED_SUBDOMAINS`. Trusted domains bypass IP resolution entirely, the hostname is preserved in all outbound requests. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][Azure DevOps] Fixed retry transient 503 on `itemsbatch` (#3209) # Description **What** - **Azure DevOps**: opt the `itemsbatch` POST in `_get_files_by_descriptors` into the shared retry transport by passing `extensions={"retryable": True}` through a new `extensions` parameter on `HTTPBaseClient.send_request`. Scope is intentionally narrow — only this known-idempotent POST opts in; webhook creation and other non-idempotent POSTs are unaffected. ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
[Integration][Github] Add Labeled and Unlabeled to Pull Request Webhook Actions (#3237)

# Description
What -
Adds `labeled` and `unlabeled` to the `PULL_REQUEST_EVENTS` allowlist in
the GitHub integration's webhook processor
(`integrations/github/github/webhook/events.py`).

Why -
`pull_request_webhook_processor._should_process_event` checks
`event.payload.get("action") in PULL_REQUEST_EVENTS`. Without `labeled`
/ `unlabeled` in that list, Port-Ocean silently drops those webhook
events. The `labels` property on `githubPullRequest` entities is only
updated at the next `synchronize` event or scheduled
resync, which breaks real-time label-driven automations.

For comparison, `ISSUE_UPSERT_EVENTS` in the same file already includes
both `labeled` and `unlabeled`. This PR brings PR-side handling to
parity with issue-side handling.

Fixes #3236.

How -
- 2-line addition to `PULL_REQUEST_EVENTS`
- Existing test `test_validate_payload_valid` iterates `for action in
PULL_REQUEST_EVENTS` and auto-covers the new entries
- Towncrier fragment added under `improvement`

subject: [Core] Add central ssl verification settings for ocean http clients (#3258)
message:
[Core] Add central ssl verification settings for ocean http clients (#3258) - **feat(HttpClients): Refactor HTTP client creation and enhance SSL settings handling** - **feat(env): Update GitLab v2 example environment file to include SSL inspection setting for Python 3.13+** # Description ## What Adds structured SSL configuration to Ocean core and applies it at the HTTP client layer: - New config: `ssl.port` and `ssl.third_party`, each with `verify` (bool) and `x509.strict` (bool). - New helpers: `resolve_verify_param()`, `create_third_party_http_client()`. - Wired into Port API client, shared `http_async_client`, and **gitlab-v2**’s base client. - Startup warnings when non-default SSL settings are used. **Defaults are unchanged** (`verify=true`, `x509.strict=true`) — same behavior as httpx’s default `verify=True` today. ## Why Users behind SSL inspection proxies can hit TLS failures on **Python 3.13+** when re-signed certs lack **AKI (Authority Key Identifier)**. OpenSSL 3 enforces that via `VERIFY_X509_STRICT`. We need a safe middle ground: - **Not** turning off TLS entirely (`verify=false`). - **Yes** relaxing only strict X.509 checks while still validating certs and hostnames (`x509.strict=false`). Central settings avoid ad-hoc env vars and inconsistent per-integration `verify_ssl` flags. ## How | Piece | Role | |-------|------| | `SslSettings` in `port_ocean/config/settings.py` | Pydantic models; env via `OCEAN__SSL__*` (e.g. `OCEAN__SSL__THIRD_PARTY__X509__STRICT=false`) | | `port_ocean/helpers/ssl.py` | Maps settings → httpx `verify`: `False`, `True`, or custom `SSLContext` with `VERIFY_X509_STRICT` cleared | | `port_ocean/helpers/http_client_factory.py` | `create_third_party_http_client()` applies `ssl.third_party` unless caller passes `verify=` | | `port_ocean/clients/port/utils.py` | Port API singleton uses `ssl.port` | | `port_ocean/utils/async_http.py` | Shared third-party client uses factory | | `port_ocean/ocean.py` | Logs warnings on startup for non-default `ssl.port` / `ssl.third_party` | | `integrations/gitlab-v2/.../base_client.py` | Switched from raw `OceanAsyncClient` to factory | `resolve_custom_integration_verify()` is added for a future **custom** integration migration (not wired in this PR). ## Configuration (reviewer cheat sheet) | Env var | Effect | |---------|--------| | `OCEAN__SSL__PORT__VERIFY=false` | Disable TLS verification for **Port API** | | `OCEAN__SSL__PORT__X509__STRICT=false` | Port API: verify certs/hostname, relax AKI strict check | | `OCEAN__SSL__THIRD_PARTY__VERIFY=false` | Disable TLS verification for third-party HTTP | | `OCEAN__SSL__THIRD_PARTY__X509__STRICT=false` | Third-party: verify certs/hostname, relax AKI strict check | Target fix for `gitlab-v2`: `OCEAN__SSL__THIRD_PARTY__X509__STRICT=false`. ## Which integrations are affected ### All integrations (Port API traffic) Every integration talks to Port via `PortClient` → `port_ocean/clients/port/utils.py`. - **Respects:** `OCEAN__SSL__PORT__*` - **Default:** no change unless env vars are set ### Third-party traffic — affected in this PR These paths use `create_third_party_http_client()` or `http_async_client` and **respect `OCEAN__SSL__THIRD_PARTY__*`**: | Integration | How wired | |-------------|-----------| | amplication | `http_async_client` | | aikido | `http_async_client` | | argocd | `http_async_client` (secure mode; insecure still uses `verify=False` explicitly) | | armorcode | `http_async_client` | | backstage | `http_async_client` | | bitbucket-cloud | `http_async_client` | | bitbucket-server | `http_async_client` | | checkmarx-one | `http_async_client` | | claude | `http_async_client` | | datadog | `http_async_client` | | dynatrace | `http_async_client` | | fake-integration | `http_async_client` | | firehydrant | `http_async_client` | | gcp | `http_async_client` (via `gcp_core/utils.py`) | | github-copilot | `http_async_client` | | jenkins | `http_async_client` | | jira-server | `http_async_client` | | komodor | `http_async_client` | | kubecost | `http_async_client` | | linear | `http_async_client` | | octopus | `http_async_client` | | okta | `http_async_client` | | opencost | `http_async_client` | | opsgenie | `http_async_client` | | servicenow | `http_async_client` (main client; OAuth helper still uses raw `OceanAsyncClient`) | | sonarqube | `http_async_client` | | statuspage | `http_async_client` | | terraform-cloud | `http_async_client` | | wiz | `http_async_client` | ### Third-party traffic — not affected yet Still construct `OceanAsyncClient` directly; subject: [Integration][Github] Fix GitHub Integration OOM by Sub batching Repository Enrichment (#3263)
message:
[Integration][Github] Fix GitHub Integration OOM by Sub batching Repository Enrichment (#3263) # Description **What** - Sub-batches repository enrichment during resync to prevent out-of-memory crashes **Why** - Large organizations (e.g. BCP with 8GB+ RAM spikes) trigger OOM kills because all repositories in a page (up to 100) are enriched concurrently via a single `asyncio.gather`, causing unbounded memory accumulation from collaborator data **How** - Introduces `ENRICHMENT_BATCH_SIZE = 10` and a `_enrich_in_batches` method that slices repos into sub-batches of 10 before calling `asyncio.gather`. Each sub-batch is yielded independently so downstream consumers can process and release memory incrementally. Uses `copy.deepcopy` on each repo before enrichment to prevent the `@cache_iterator_result` decorator from retaining references to enriched (heavy) objects. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

message:
Task tfqko7/rc release improvements (#3283)

## Description

### What
- Updated `release-rc` workflow to support integration-only RC releases
without forcing core release steps.
- Fixed integration-only image tag format from
`rc-{integration-version}-rc{N}` to `{integration-version}-rc{N}`.
- Fixed RC summary output to render concrete Docker image tags (no
template placeholders) and list all selected integrations.
- Added `.DS_Store` to `.gitignore` and removed tracked `.DS_Store` from
the repo.

### Why
- We needed to test and publish integration RC images (e.g. Datadog)
from feature branches without publishing a core PyPI RC or creating a
GitHub core tag/release when `port_ocean/` is unchanged.
- The previous summary text was misleading because it showed unresolved
placeholders instead of real image tags.
- Repository hygiene: prevent macOS `.DS_Store` files from polluting git
history.

### How
- Detect core changes vs merge-base with `main` using
`tj-actions/changed-files`.
- Gate core jobs (`publish-core-rc`, `tag-source-branch`) behind
`core_changed == true`.
- Keep integration matrix/build running independently so
integration-only branches still produce images.
- Compute Docker tags by mode:
- core changed:
`ghcr.io/port-labs/port-ocean-<integration>:rc-<core-version-rcN>`
- integration-only:
`ghcr.io/port-labs/port-ocean-<integration>:<integration-version-rcN>`

integrations and their `pyproject.toml` versions.

subject: [Core] Fix 401 from port-api cause resync to fail (#3286)
message:
[Core] Fix 401 from port-api cause resync to fail (#3286) # Description Problem: During long resyncs, Ocean keeps using a cached Port access token (last_token_object) for API calls such as POST /v1/entities/search. Port may return 401 with "token is expired" while Ocean still treats the token as valid locally (last_token_object.expired is false), because local expiry is based on expiresIn and fetch time, which can differ from the JWT’s actual lifetime on Port’s side. When that happened, retries did not recover: Token refresh often did not run, because refresh was tied to the local expired flag. Even when refresh ran, the new token was written to response.headers, but retries resend the original request, so the stale Authorization header was reused. subject: [Integration][Azure-DevOps] Filter webhook subscriptions by event type to prevent timeouts in large organizations (#3294)
message:
[Integration][Azure-DevOps] Filter webhook subscriptions by event type to prevent timeouts in large organizations (#3294) # Description What - Filter the GET /_apis/hooks/subscriptions call by publisherId and eventType when fetching existing webhook subscriptions during setup. Fetch once per organization (before the project loop) and reuse the result across all projects. Why - On large ADO orgs, the unfiltered subscriptions call consistently times out at 60s the response is 12–13 MB. This means webhook setup never completes, so live events never arrive. Filtering reduces each call to ~546 KB and the 23 event-type calls run in parallel via asyncio.gather, completing in ~11s total. Caching the result eliminates per-project redundancy (previously N×23 calls, now 23 calls once per org). How - - Added publisher_id / event_type params to generate_subscriptions_webhook_events() for filtered fetches - Added get_filtered_webhook_subscriptions() which derives unique (publisherId, eventType) pairs from AZURE_DEVOPS_WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTIONS and fires them in parallel with asyncio.gather - setup.py now calls get_filtered_webhook_subscriptions() once before the project loop and passes existing_subscriptions into every create_webhook_subscriptions() call ## Type of change Please leave one option from the following and delete the rest: - [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
